Head: Logic
Path: 一. Logic
Gloss: The structure of reality and, in the same concepts, of thought: the basic determinations all thinking relies on, each leading to the next. Then the study of these concepts in their own right and in that order.
Hegelian gloss: The science of the pure idea, of thought as the self-movement of the concept, in which the determinations of thought are at once the determinations of things.
Nouns: logic, science of logic; speculative logic, dialectical logic, objective logic, subjective logic; dialectic, dialectics; science of thought, science of pure reason; pure thought; thinking, ratiocination &c (inference) H0175. metaphysics, first philosophy, ontology, theory of categories; table of categories. thought thinking itself; reason; realm of shadows; the system of pure reason; categories, predicaments†, forms of thought. the system of categories. logomachy, noesis.
Verbs: think, reason, ratiocinate, cogitate, excogitate†; think through, think out, follow out, carry through; reason a priori; categorize; deduce, derive, develop, unfold; logicize, syllogize &c H0175. reflect. draw an inference.
Adjective: logical, dialectical, speculative, categorial, ontological, metaphysical; pure, formal, abstract; presuppositionless; rational, noetic, intelligible; systematic, immanent, self-developing. reflective. intellectual, mental.
Adverbs: logically, dialectically &c adj.; in thought, in pure thought, in the element of thought.
Foreign: German: Wissenschaft der Logik, das reine Denken, Vernunft, Reich der Schatten, Denkformen, voraussetzungslos, das Logische, Zahl, Erzählung, liegen, lesen; Latin: prima philosophia, ratio, a priori, in abstracto, sub specie aeternitatis, oratio, verbum; Greek: organon, logos, noēsis noēseōs, nous; Arabic: manṭiq; Sanskrit: nyāya, hetuvidyā, pramāṇa [means of valid knowledge]; Chinese: mingjia [School of Names]; Korean: nollihak [logic], sabyeon [speculation]; French: discours, langage, langue, parole, rationalité, raison, intelligence, fondement, principe, motif, proportion, calcul, rapport, relation, récit, thèse, raisonnement, argument, explication, énoncé, proposition, phrase, définition, compte, conte; Hebrew: davar.
Phrases: to gar auto noein estin te kai einai [Gr.] [Parmenides]; noēsis noēseōs [Gr.] [Aristotle]; the exposition of God as he is in his eternal essence before the creation of nature and a finite mind [Hegel]; what is rational is actual, and what is actual is rational [Hegel]; the logic of things; the long and the short of it.
Hegel definition: Logic is the science of pure thought, the system of pure reason, truth as it is in and for itself. It cannot presuppose its forms, its rules, its method or even the concept of itself, since all these belong to its content and must be established within it, so that it can say what it is only as the result of its whole treatment. Its determinations are not empty forms set over against a content given from elsewhere: the necessary forms of thinking are the content and the truth itself.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· Introduction
Hegel citations:
Logic, on the contrary, cannot presuppose any of these forms of reflection, these rules and laws of thinking, for they are part of its content and they first have to be established within it.
— The Science of Logic, Introduction (tr. di Giovanni)
Accordingly, logic is to be understood as the system of pure reason, as the realm of pure thought. This realm is truth unveiled, truth as it is in and for itself.
— The Science of Logic, Introduction (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Doctrine of Being
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being
Gloss: The study of the simplest concepts, those that describe a thing directly as it is, without reference to anything behind it. Each such concept, when thought through, gives way to another.
Hegelian gloss: The sphere of immediacy, where each determination simply is and passes over into another; the concept only in itself.
Nouns: doctrine of being; logic of being, ontology; immediacy, directness, givenness, the given, datum, data; surface, face value; transition, passing over; change into another &c (becoming) H0007, rectilinearity†. the in-itself; being-in-itself; the concept in itself, latency, implicitness, potentiality; first sphere, outset, threshold. categories of being, immediate categories; what simply is, what there is; brute fact, plain fact, bare fact. beginning, commencement, inception. the sphere of immediacy, quality quantity and measure. esse, ens.
Verbs: be, exist, obtain, be given, lie to hand; pass over, pass into, go over into, turn into, give way to, change into; follow upon; lie on the surface. have being, subsist. become.
Adjective: immediate, unmediated, direct, given, simple, bare, plain, raw; ontic, ontological, existential; implicit, latent, potential, inchoate, rudimentary, undeveloped; transitional, transitive, passing, transient; first, initial, primary, elementary. mere, sheer.
Adverbs: immediately, directly, simply, barely, at first sight, at face value, on the face of it; in itself; in the first instance.
Foreign: German: Seinslogik, Unmittelbarkeit, Übergehen, Übergang, das Ansich, Ansichsein, an sich; Latin: prima facie; Greek: metabasis; Korean: jonjaeron [ontology].
Phrases: panta rhei [Gr.] [attrib. Heraclitus]; what is, is; in the nature of things; the way of all flesh.
Hegel definition: The doctrine of being is the first book of the Logic, in which being is considered as the indeterminate immediate and as the sphere within which its own determinations and the movement of its reflection fall. It is one sphere of the concept, set off against essence. In it being posits itself in three determinations: as determinateness, that is quality; as sublated determinateness, magnitude or quantity; and as qualitatively determined quantity, measure.

Hegel citations:

— The Science of Logic, The Doctrine of Being (tr. di Giovanni)
In this, being will posit itself in three determinations: I. as determinateness; as such, quality; II. as sublated determinateness; magnitude, quantity; III. as qualitatively determined quantity; measure.
— The Science of Logic, The Doctrine of Being (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Determinateness (Quality)
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality)
Gloss: The character that makes a thing what it is, so that if the character changes the thing becomes something else; the most basic kind of definiteness.
Hegelian gloss: Determinateness immediately one with being, so that a thing ceases to be what it is when its quality changes.
Nouns: quality; determinateness, definiteness, determination; character, characteristic, nature, kind, sort, type, stamp, cast, complexion, constitution, make, make-up, grain, fibre, temper, mettle; essence &c (essence) H0088; whatness, quiddity, haecceity, thisness, so-being; identity of kind. property, attribute, trait, mark, note, feature, earmark, hallmark, signature; idiosyncrasy, peculiarity, specificity. qualitative difference, difference in kind; such-and-suchness, suchness. lineament. speciality, particularity. determinacy, definite character, qualitative determinateness. trademark. quale, talis.
Verbs: qualify, characterize, specify, determine, define, distinguish, differentiate, mark, stamp, brand, tinge, colour; be of a kind, partake of; have the character of; be such as, be such that.
Adjective: qualitative, qualitied, qualified, characteristic, distinctive, specific, peculiar, proper, typical, idiosyncratic; determinate, definite, determined; essential, constitutive, intrinsic, inherent, innate, ingrained, inborn; such, of a kind, of a sort. particular.
Adverbs: qualitatively, characteristically &c adj.; in kind, in nature; essentially, intrinsically; by nature; as such. determinately.
Foreign: German: Bestimmtheit, Sosein; Latin: qualitas, quidditas, per se; Greek: poiotēs; Sanskrit: guṇa [quality, strand of nature], tathatā; Chinese: xing [nature, inborn character].
Phrases: qualis artifex pereo [Lat.] [Nero]; a leopard cannot change his spots; naturam expellas furca, tamen usque recurret [Lat.] [Horace]; such as it is.
Hegel definition: Determinateness, or quality, is the first section of the doctrine of being. Being as the indeterminate immediate is free of determinateness, being without quality; yet its indeterminateness belongs to it only in opposition to what is determinate, and so itself constitutes its quality. The first being thus shows itself determinate in itself and passes into existence; existence, as finite, sublates itself into the infinite reference of being to itself, and passes into being-for-itself.

· The Doctrine of Being › Determinateness (Quality)
Hegel citations:
Being is the indeterminate immediate; it is free of determinateness with respect to essence, just as it is still free of any determinateness that it can receive within itself.
— The Science of Logic, Determinateness (Quality) (tr. di Giovanni)
Determinate being thus comes to stand over and against being in general; with that, however, the very indeterminateness of being constitutes its quality.
— The Science of Logic, Determinateness (Quality) (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Being
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › α. Being
Gloss: The bare fact of existence, considered before anything is said about what exists.
Hegelian gloss: The first beginning of the logic: indeterminate immediacy, which proves to be the same as nothing and passes into becoming.
Nouns: being; existence &c (determinate being) H0013, isness, is-ness, thereness; the that, that-it-is. the bare fact of existence; the first, the beginning, the starting point, the point of departure; the immediate, the undetermined; the indeterminate; the simple; the absolute beginning. the copula, "is". existence, entity, subsistence. the is, bare existence, the fact of being. inchoation, incipience.
Verbs: be, exist, subsist, obtain, be there, be the case; begin, start, commence &c (beginning) H0222; set out, take one's departure. have being, occur &c H0116, have place, prevail.
Adjective: being, existent, existing, extant; simple, bare, sheer, mere, pure, immediate; indeterminate, undetermined, indefinite, featureless; first, initial, primordial, primal, aboriginal, original, primitive, elementary, rudimentary; abstract, empty. under the sun, in existence, undestroyed, unsuppressed†.
Adverbs: simply, barely, merely; at first, in the beginning, at the outset.
Foreign: Latin: esse, ens, quod est, terminus a quo, principium, ab initio, ab ovo, in principio, univocitas entis [univocity of being] [Duns Scotus]; Greek: to on, einai, archē; Arabic: wujūd [existence, being]; Sanskrit: sat [being, the real]; Chinese: you [being, having].
Phrases: esti gar einai [Gr.] [Parmenides]; in the beginning was the Word [Bible]; to be or not to be, that is the question [Hamlet]; ex nihilo nihil fit [Lat.]; from the ground up; ens rationis [Lat.]; ergo sum cogito [Lat.], thinkest thou existence doth depend on time? [Byron].
Hegel definition: Being is the first chapter and the beginning of the Logic, the sphere of being, nothing and becoming. Pure being, taken without any further determination, proves to be nothing, and nothing the same as being; their truth is the movement in which each vanishes into the other, becoming, which collapses into existence. Hegel recalls the Eleatics, Parmenides above all, as the first to give voice to the simple thought of pure being as the sole truth.

Hegel citations:
The Eleatics were the first to give voice to the simple thought of pure being – notable among them Parmenides, who declared it to be the absolute and sole truth.
— The Science of Logic, Being, Remark (tr. di Giovanni)

— The Science of Logic, Being, Remark (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Pure Being
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › α. Being › a. Pure Being
Gloss: Existence with no further content at all; "is" without any "what." So empty that nothing definite can be thought in it.
Hegelian gloss: Being, pure being, without any further determination: indeterminate immediacy, equal only to itself, with nothing to be intuited or thought in it.
Nouns: pure being; being as such, being qua being; mere being, bare being, naked being, sheer existence; indeterminate immediacy; the empty, the void &c H0006, emptiness, vacancy, blankness, vacuity, inanity; abstraction, the abstract, highest genus; the One of Parmenides, the Eleatic One. [Modern] being in general, Being. sheer being, indeterminate being, the empty is. isness.
Verbs: be simply, be purely, merely be; abstract from everything, prescind, strip away, empty out; be equal only to oneself. be.
Adjective: pure, sheer, mere, bare, naked, simple, unalloyed, unqualified, unconditioned; indeterminate, undetermined, undifferentiated, indistinct, featureless, characterless, contentless, empty, void, vacant, blank, vacuous, inane; abstract, general; self-same, self-equal; ineffable, unsayable, unthinkable. empty &c H0237, null. homogeneous.
Adverbs: purely, simply, merely, barely; as such, qua being.
Foreign: German: unbestimmte Unmittelbarkeit, Sein überhaupt, das reine Sein; Latin: esse purum, esse simpliciter, ens qua ens, summum genus, ens generalissimum, ens commune [scholastic], simpliciter, tabula rasa; Greek: on hē on; Sanskrit: sanmātra [pure being], nirguṇa [without qualities]; Chinese: wuji [the limitless]; French: il y a [anonymous being, before any existent] [Levinas].
Phrases: the same thing exists for thinking and for being [Parmenides]; esse est percipi [Lat.] [Berkeley]; ens et unum convertuntur [Lat.]; the bare fact.
Hegel definition: Pure being is the beginning of the Logic: being without any further determination. It is immediacy with nothing indeterminate about it left over to be fixed, equal only to itself and not even unequal to anything else, with no difference inside it or outward. Any content would take away its purity. There is therefore nothing in it to intuit or to think; it is only empty intuiting or empty thinking itself. Precisely as this indeterminate immediacy, being is in fact nothing, neither more nor less.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Being › Being
Hegel citations:
Being, pure being – without further determination. In its indeterminate immediacy it is equal only to itself and also not unequal with respect to another; it has no difference within it, nor any outwardly.
— The Science of Logic, Being › Being (tr. di Giovanni)
It is pure indeterminateness and emptiness. – There is nothing to be intuited in it, if one can speak here of intuiting; or, it is only this pure empty intuiting itself. Just as little is anything to be thought in it, or, it is equally only this empty thinking. Being, the indeterminate immediate is in fact nothing, and neither more nor less than nothing.
— The Science of Logic, Being › Being (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Pure Nothing
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › α. Being › b. Pure Nothing
Gloss: The complete absence of anything; emptiness taken as the opposite of being, yet just as blank and indefinite.
Hegelian gloss: Nothing, pure nothing: simple equality with itself, complete emptiness, absence of all determination; the same as pure being.

Hegel definition: Pure nothing is simple equality with itself, complete emptiness, the complete absence of determination and content, without any distinction within it. It is not mere absence in the loose sense: it makes a difference whether something or nothing is intuited or thought, so nothing is in our intuiting and thinking, as the empty intuiting and thinking itself. It thus has the same determination, or rather lack of determination, as pure being, and is altogether the same as what pure being is.

To intuit or to think nothing has therefore a meaning; the two are distinguished and so nothing is (concretely exists) in our intuiting or thinking; or rather it is the empty intuiting and thinking itself, like pure being. – Nothing is therefore the same determination or rather absence of determination, and thus altogether the same as what pure being is.
— The Science of Logic, Being › Nothing (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Becoming
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › α. Being › c. Becoming
Gloss: Change at its most basic: the passing of being into nothing and of nothing into being. The first concept with real content, since it holds both together.
Hegelian gloss: The truth of being and nothing: the movement in which each has already passed over into the other, their immediate vanishing in one another.

Foreign: German: Unruhe; Latin: fieri, in fieri; Greek: genesis, gignesthai, kinēsis; Sanskrit: anitya, saṃsāra; Pali: anicca; Chinese: yi [change]; Japanese: mujō [impermanence]; Korean: saengseong [becoming]; French: devenir [Deleuze].
Phrases: panta rhei [Gr.] [attrib. Heraclitus]; you cannot step twice into the same river [Heraclitus]; omnia mutantur, nihil interit [Lat.] [Ovid]; tempora mutantur, nos et mutamur in illis [Lat.]; plus ça change, plus c'est la même chose [Fr.] [Alphonse Karr]; all things flow; a change came o'er the spirit of my dream [Byron]; nous avons change tout cela [Moliere]; tempora mutantur nos et mutamur in illis [Lat.]; non sum qualis eram [Lat.] [Horace]; casaque tourner [Fr.]; corpora lente augescent cito extinguuntur [Tacitus]; in statu quo ante bellum [Lat.]; still ending and beginning still [Cowper]; vox audita perit littera scripta manet [Lat.]; pictra mossa non fa muschis [It.]; honores mutant mores [Lat.]; varium et mutabile semper femina [Lat.] [Virgil].
Hegel definition: Becoming is the truth of pure being and pure nothing. They are the same, and yet absolutely distinct; neither stays what it is, for being has already passed over into nothing and nothing into being. Their truth is the movement in which each immediately vanishes into its opposite: a movement in which the two are distinguished, but by a distinction that dissolves itself as soon as it is made. Becoming is the first concrete thought of the Logic, in which being and nothing have their being only as vanishing.

Hegel citations:

— The Science of Logic, Being › Becoming (tr. di Giovanni)
Their truth is therefore this movement of the immediate vanishing of the one into the other: becoming, a movement in which the two are distinguished, but by a distinction which has just as immediately dissolved itself.
— The Science of Logic, Being › Becoming (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Unity of Being and Nothing
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › α. Being › c. Becoming › i. Unity of Being and Nothing
Gloss: The fact that being and nothing, though opposites, cannot be held apart: each turns into the other as soon as it is thought.
Hegelian gloss: Being and nothing are the same, and yet absolutely distinct; their unity is not a resting identity but becoming.

Adjective: one and the same, identical, coincident, coincidental; inseparable, indissoluble, indissociable, inextricable; paradoxical, antinomic, antinomical, contradictory; nondual, advaitic, indissolvable†, infrangible†. united.
Adverbs: at one, as one, together, conjointly, inseparably; at once, at the same stroke; in the same breath. at the same time, simultaneously. immediately.
Foreign: German: Verschwinden; Latin: coincidentia oppositorum [Cusanus], concordia discors, discordia concors, uno ictu; Sanskrit: advaita [nonduality]; Chinese: yinyang, taiji [supreme polarity].
Phrases: the way up and the way down are one and the same [Heraclitus]; coincidentia oppositorum [Lat.] [Cusanus]; extremes meet; les extrêmes se touchent [Fr.]; the same and not the same; neither one thing nor the other.
Hegel definition: The unity of being and nothing says that pure being and pure nothing are the same. This sameness is not a rest in which the difference has disappeared. Being and nothing are absolutely distinct, yet equally unseparated and inseparable. What is true is neither of them taken alone, but that each has passed over into the other. The proposition "being and nothing are the same" is therefore one-sided if it leaves out their difference; what states the matter adequately is their movement into one another, which is becoming.

Hegel citations:

— The Science of Logic, Becoming › Unity of being and nothing (tr. di Giovanni)
But the truth is just as much that they are not without distinction; it is rather that they are not the same, that they are absolutely distinct yet equally unseparated and inseparable

Head: Moments of Becoming
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › α. Being › c. Becoming › ii. Moments of Becoming
Gloss: The two directions of becoming, coming-to-be and ceasing-to-be, each passing into the other.
Hegelian gloss: The moments of becoming: coming-to-be, where nothing passes into being, and ceasing-to-be, where being passes into nothing; each sublates itself in itself.
Nouns: moments of becoming; appearance, dawn; creation, production. generation and corruption; arising and passing away, rise and fall, ebb and flow, waxing and waning, flux and reflux; birth and death, life and death; the wheel of becoming.
Verbs: appear, dawn; produce. wax and wane, ebb and flow, rise and fall. pass, go, avaunt†, vaporize, be gone, leave no trace, leave 'not a rack behind' [Tempest], go off the stage &c H0238, suffer an eclipse, undergo an eclipse, retire from sight, be lost to view, pass out of sight.

Foreign: German: Vergehen; Latin: generatio, corruptio, generatio et corruptio, in ovo, in articulo mortis; Greek: genesis, phthora, genesis kai phthora; Sanskrit: utpāda [arising], nirodha [cessation], bhavacakra; Chinese: shengmie [arising and extinction].
Phrases: mors janua vitae [Lat.]; what's past is prologue [Tempest]; coming and going; here today, gone tomorrow; let's get going!, let's get this show on the road!, up and at 'em!; aller Anfang ist schwer [Ger.], dimidium facti qui coepit habet [Lat.] [Cicero]; as high as Heaven and as deep as hell [Beaumont and Fletcher]; en toute chose il faut considerer la fin [Fr.]; finem respice [Lat.]; ultimus Romanorum [Lat.]; I pause for a reply [Julius Caesar].
Hegel definition: Becoming contains being and nothing not in abstraction but as moments of a determinate unity in which each is only as vanishing, as sublated. Each of them is itself a unity with the other, so becoming is doubly determined. Where nothing is the immediate and refers to being, it is coming-to-be; where being is the immediate and passes into nothing, it is ceasing-to-be. The two are one becoming. As opposed directions they interpenetrate and check each other, and neither is sublated from outside: each sublates itself and is in itself its opposite.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Being › Becoming › The moments of becoming
Hegel citations:
Becoming is the unseparatedness of being and nothing, not the unity that abstracts from being and nothing; as the unity of being and nothing it is rather this determinate unity, or one in which being and nothing equally are. However, inasmuch as being and nothing are each unseparated from its other, each is not. In this unity, therefore, they are, but as vanishing, only as sublated. They sink from their initially represented self-subsistence into moments which are still distinguished but at the same time sublated.
— The Science of Logic, Becoming › The moments of becoming (tr. di Giovanni)
Becoming is in this way doubly determined. Head: Sublation

Hegel definition: Here, in becoming, Hegel gives an account of sublation at this early stage: the sublation of becoming is the collapse of the unrest of becoming into a quiet result. Becoming rests on the distinction of being and nothing, yet what it unites is opposed to itself, and such a union destroys itself. When being and nothing vanish, the vanishing itself vanishes. What results is not nothing, which would only be a relapse into one of the sublated moments, but the unity of being and nothing become quiescent simplicity. As being that is now determined by this whole, it is existence. It is not mere being, but being with a non-being taken up into it, so that the whole has determinateness. Hegel definition: Existence as such is existence taken first by itself, before it stands in relation to an other. — The Science of Logic, Finitude › Something and an other (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Determination, Constitution, and Limit
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › ii. Determination, Constitution, and Limit
Gloss: Three ways a thing is defined: its determination, what it is essentially; its constitution, what it happens to be through outside circumstance; and its limit, the boundary where it stops and something else begins.
Hegelian gloss: Determination, what something is in itself; constitution, what it is through its relation to other; limit, the non-being of each in the other.
Nouns: determination, constitution, and limit.
Adjective: qualifying, qualified, hedged, conditional, exceptional &c H0073.
Foreign: German: Beschaffenheit, Grenze; Latin: finis, terminus; Greek: telos, peras [limit]; Arabic: ḥadd; Korean: gyujeong [determination], hangye [limit].
Phrases: est modus in rebus, sunt certi denique fines [Lat.] [Horace].
Hegel definition: Determination, constitution and limit are the ways in which something, having taken its being-for-other back into its being-in-itself, holds its otherness within itself. Determination is the in-itself by which something preserves itself while involved with an other; constitution is what in it is exposed to external influence and relation. Each passes over into the other. Since the otherness is now posited within something as its own moment, there are two somethings that negate and join each other through one determinateness, and this is limit.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Existence › Finitude › Determination, constitution, and limit
Hegel citations:
The in-itself, in which the something is reflected into itself from its being-for-other, no longer is an abstract in-itself but, as the negation of its being-for-other, is mediated through this latter, which is thus its moment.
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › Determination, constitution, and limit (tr. di Giovanni)
Determination and constitution are thus distinct from each other; something, according to its determination, is indifferent to its constitution.
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › Determination, constitution, and limit (tr. di Giovanni)
It is one determinateness of the two somethings that, on the one hand, as negation of the negation, is identical with the in-itselfness of the somethings, and also, on the other hand, since these negations are to each other as other somethings, joins them together of their own accord and, since each negation negates the other, equally separates them. This determinateness is limit.
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › Determination, constitution, and limit (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Determination
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › ii. Determination, Constitution, and Limit › 1. Determination
Gloss: What something is in itself and is meant to be; its vocation, kept up in its relation to others.
Hegelian gloss: Bestimmung, the in-itself of something filled with content and maintained against its relation to other.
Nouns: determination. vocation, destiny, calling, purpose, end, in-itself, inner nature. destination, what something is meant to be, the vocation of man.
Verbs: determine, destine, ordain, appoint, fix.
Adjective: determined, destined, fated, intended.
Adverbs: by nature.
Phrases: die Bestimmung des Menschen [Ger.] [Fichte].
Hegel definition: Determination is affirmative determinateness: the in-itself by which something abides in its existence while involved with an other that would determine it, preserving its self-equality and holding on to it in its being-for-other. Something fulfils its determination in so far as the further determinateness that comes to it through its relation to the other becomes its filling. So what something is in itself is also present in it. The determination, or vocation, of the human being is rational thought, which is at first only in itself, as an ought.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Existence › Finitude › Determination, constitution, and limit
Hegel citations:
Determination is affirmative determinateness; it is the in-itself by which a something abides in its existence while involved with an other that would determine it, by which it preserves itself in its self-equality, holding on to it in its being-for-other.
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › Determination, constitution, and limit (tr. di Giovanni)
The determination of the human being, its vocation, is rational thought: thinking in general is his simple determinateness
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › Determination, constitution, and limit (tr. di Giovanni)
Determination implies that what something is in itself is also present in it.
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › Determination, constitution, and limit (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Constitution
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › ii. Determination, Constitution, and Limit › 2. Constitution
Gloss: What something happens to be through its circumstances and its dealings with other things.
Hegelian gloss: Beschaffenheit, the determinateness something has through its being-for-other: its outward make-up, open to influence and alteration.
Nouns: constitution. make-up, condition, state, circumstance, situation, disposition, external character, accidental nature. habitude, diathesis†, fabric &c H0268, stamp, set, fit, mold, mould. category, estate, lot, mood, temper, aspect &c H0418, dilemma, pass, predicament. phase, position, posture, attitude, place, point, terms, regime, footing, standing, status.
Verbs: constitute, condition, dispose, frame, shape.
Adjective: constituted, conditioned, circumstanced, situated.
Adverbs: by circumstance.
Hegel definition: Constitution is the determinateness that belongs to something as external existence: what it has in it, but not as part of its being-in-itself. Constituted in this or that way, something is caught up in external influences and relationships, which appear accidental, although it is the quality of something to be given over to them. When something alters, the alteration falls on its constitution, the unstable surface of its otherness, while the something preserves itself and its determination is left untouched, until the two pass into one another.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Existence › Finitude › Determination, constitution, and limit
Hegel citations:
Constituted in this or that way, the something is caught up in external influences and in external relationships. This external connection on which the constitution depends, and the being determined through an other, appear as something accidental. But it is the quality of the something to be given over to this externality and to have a constitution.
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › Determination, constitution, and limit (tr. di Giovanni)
In so far as something alters, the alteration falls on the side of its constitution; the latter is that in the something which becomes an other. The something itself preserves itself in the alteration; the latter affects only this unstable surface of the something’s otherness, not its determination.
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › Determination, constitution, and limit (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Limit
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › ii. Determination, Constitution, and Limit › 3. Limit
Gloss: The point where something stops and something else begins, which both separates and joins them.
Hegelian gloss: Grenze, the non-being of the other in something and of something in the other, through which something is what it is and also is not.
Nouns: limit. boundary, border, bound, bourn†, frontier, edge, margin, brink, verge, rim, periphery, confines, pale, march, marches, terminus, term, horizon, ceiling, threshold, line, demarcation, delimitation, circumscription, roomage†. bounds, enclave, curbstone†, but, reservation, termination, stint, precinct, backwoods.
Verbs: limit, bound, delimit, demarcate, circumscribe, confine, restrict, hem in, fence in, wall in, draw the line, mark off, mark out. inclose, surround &c H0228, compass about, hedge in, rail in, fence round, hedge round.
Adjective: limited, bounded, bordered, circumscribed, confined, restricted, terminal, marginal, peripheral, liminal, borderline, frontier, labiated†, marginated†. definite, conterminate†, conterminable†, bordering.
Adverbs: within limits, within bounds, within the pale, at the limit, on the edge, on the verge, on the brink, up to a point, so far and no further.
Phrases: ne plus ultra [Lat.]; hitherto shalt thou come, but no further [Bible]; good fences make good neighbours [Frost].
Hegel definition: Limit is the non-being of the other, through which something is what it is. It is not only the non-being of the other but equally that of the something, so that something through its limit both is and is not. Something has its existence outside its limit, yet only in its limit does it have existence; the limit separates the two and is their common distinguishedness. In the limit something is therefore restless, a contradiction that drives it beyond itself, as the point passes into the line.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Existence › Finitude › Determination, constitution, and limit
Hegel citations:
In limiting, something is of course thereby reduced to being limited itself; but, as the ceasing of the other in it, its limit is at the same time itself only the being of the something; this something is what it is by virtue of it, has its quality in it.
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › Determination, constitution, and limit (tr. di Giovanni)
The limit is the mediation in virtue of which something and other each both is and is not.
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › Determination, constitution, and limit (tr. di Giovanni)
The other determination is the unrest of the something in its limit in which it is immanent, the contradiction that propels it beyond itself.
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › Determination, constitution, and limit (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Finitude as Such
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › iii. Finitude as Such
Gloss: Limitedness taken seriously: a thing whose limit is part of its very nature, so that it is bound to pass away; mortality, transience.
Hegelian gloss: The finite as such, whose being consists in having its limit within itself as its own end, so that its hour of birth is the hour of its death.
Nouns: finitude as such; mortality, the mortal condition, being-toward-death; perishability, transience, transitoriness, ephemerality, evanescence, fragility, frailty, vulnerability, precariousness, caducity; destined end, appointed end, doom, fate, lot; impermanence; vanity; the dust, dust and ashes; death's-head, skull, hourglass, guttering candle. finite things &c H0018. finiteness, limitedness, perishableness. terminability.
Verbs: perish, pass away, die, expire, decay, fade, wither, crumble, moulder; be numbered, have one's days numbered; be bound to die. cease to exist &c H0004, die out, disappear &c H0009. flit, vanish. end, run out.
Adjective: mortal, perishable, perishing, ephemeral, transient, fleeting, fugitive, evanescent, short-lived, momentary, frail, fragile, brittle, precarious, vulnerable; doomed, fated, foredoomed, condemned; sublunary, earthly, terrestrial, creaturely. transitory, passing. temporal, temporary, impermanent. finite.
Adverbs: in the end, at last, sooner or later; till death; for a season. finitely.
Foreign: German: Sein zum Tode, Endlichkeit; Latin: vanitas, memento mori; Hebrew: hevel [vapour, futility]; Pali: anicca; Chinese: wuchang [impermanence].
Phrases: memento mori [Lat.]; vanitas vanitatum, omnia vanitas [Lat.] [Bible]; golden lads and girls all must, as chimney-sweepers, come to dust [Cymbeline]; all that lives must die, passing through nature to eternity [Hamlet]; et in Arcadia ego [Lat.]; all good things must come to an end; one's days are numbered.
Hegel definition: Finitude as such is the quality of something whose limit is immanent in it, so that its negation constitutes its very being-in-itself. To call things finite is to say not only that they are determinate and limited, but that non-being constitutes their nature. They are, but the truth of this being is their end. Finitude is qualitative negation driven to the extreme and fixed in itself, the most obstinate category of the understanding, which makes the transitoriness of things imperishable and absolute and will not let the finite pass into its affirmative, the infinite.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Existence › Finitude › Finitude
Hegel citations:
When we say of things that they are finite, we understand by this that they not only have a determinateness, that their quality is not only reality and existent determination, that they are not merely limited and as such still have existence outside their limit, but rather that non-being constitutes their nature, their being.
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › Finitude (tr. di Giovanni)
Because of this qualitative simplicity of negation that has returned to the abstract opposition of nothing and perishing to being, finitude is the most obstinate of the categories of the understanding; negation in general, constitution, limit, are compatible with their other, with existence; even the abstract nothing, by itself, is given up as an abstraction; but finitude is negation fixed in itself and, as such, stands in stark contrast to its affirmative.
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › Finitude (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: The Immediacy of Finitude
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › iii. Finitude as Such › 1. The Immediacy of Finitude
Gloss: The limited thing as simply given: something whose very being is to perish.
Hegelian gloss: The finite in its immediacy, determined only to perish, its passing away fixed as its unalterable being.
Nouns: immediacy of finitude; the merely finite, sheer finitude, bare mortality; fixed finitude, hardened finitude, the finite as absolute; despair of the finite, melancholy, sadness, mourning; perishing as essence; fatalism, resignation, acceptance of mortality; nothingness of the finite, nullity, vanity &c H0024. immediate finitude, the perishable, perishing, the hour of birth as the hour of death, the given finite. perishability, transience, caducity.
Verbs: be merely finite, be nothing but mortal; perish, waste away; insist on finitude, hold fast to the finite, cling to the finite. pass away, cease.
Adjective: merely finite, purely mortal, irredeemably finite; ephemeral, fleeting; melancholy, mournful, elegiac, resigned, fatalistic, epicedial†. transient, transitory, passing. perishable, immediate.
Adverbs: merely, only, no more than; in the end; irrevocably, without remedy. transiently, perishably.
Phrases: all is vanity and vexation of spirit [Bible]; out, out, brief candle [Macbeth]; sunt lacrimae rerum et mentem mortalia tangunt [Lat.] [Virgil]; born to die; the end of the line.
Hegel definition: The immediacy of the finite is finitude taken in its simplest form, as qualitative negation returned to the abstract opposition of perishing and nothing to being. Things are left with no affirmative being apart from their determination to ruin. The finite may be put into flux, for that it should end is its only determination, but it refuses to be brought affirmatively to its affirmative, the infinite. So held, its finitude is eternal. The development of finitude shows, however, that the finite collapses within itself as this contradiction, and that perishing itself perishes.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Existence › Finitude › Finitude › The immediacy of finitude
Hegel citations:
The thought of the finitude of things brings this mournful note with it because finitude is qualitative negation driven to the extreme, and in the simplicity of such a determination there is no longer left to things an affirmative being distinct from their determination as things destined to ruin.
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › The immediacy of finitude (tr. di Giovanni)
The development of the finite will show that, expressly as this contradiction, it collapses internally, but that, in this collapse, it actually resolves the contradiction; it will show that the finite is not just perishable, and that it perishes, but that the perishing, the nothing, is rather not the last of it; that the perishing rather perishes.
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › The immediacy of finitude (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Restriction and the Ought
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › iii. Finitude as Such › 2. Restriction and the Ought
Gloss: The limit felt as a barrier to be overcome, and the demand to overcome it. What a thing ought to be stands against what it is.
Hegelian gloss: The limit as a restriction (Schranke) within something, and the ought (Sollen) that is to go beyond it; each implies the other.
Nouns: restriction and the ought; bond. coercion &c H0712, cohibition†, repression, suppression, discipline, control.
Adjective: windbound†.
Foreign: German: das Sollen, Streben, Sehnsucht; Latin: nisus, de jure; Sanskrit: dharma [duty]; Chinese: dao [the way one ought to go]; Korean: dangwi [the ought]; French: devoir.
Phrases: ad astra per aspera [Lat.]; thus far and no further; occurrent nubes [Lat.].
Hegel definition: Restriction and the ought are the two moments of the finite. Something's own limit, posited by it as a negative that is at the same time essential, is a restriction; and its being-in-itself, as negative reference to that limit as to its restriction, is the ought. For a limit to be a restriction, something must at the same time transcend it. Each is only with the other: something is raised above its restriction as ought, yet has its restriction only as ought. What ought to be both is and is not.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Existence › Finitude › Finitude › Restriction and the ought
Hegel citations:
Something’s own limit, thus posited by it as a negative which is at the same time essential, is not only limit as such, but restriction.
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › Restriction and the ought (tr. di Giovanni)
As ought something is thus elevated above its restriction, but conversely it has its restriction only as ought. The two are indivisible. Something has a restriction in so far as it has negation in its determination, and the determination is also the being sublated of the restriction.
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › Restriction and the ought (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Restriction
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › iii. Finitude as Such › 2. Restriction and the Ought › a. Restriction
Gloss: A limit felt from within as a barrier that one already reaches beyond.
Hegelian gloss: Schranke, the limit as something's own negation, posited as a restriction that its in-itself already transcends.
Nouns: restriction. limitation, barrier, bar, obstacle, check, hindrance, impediment, constraint, restraint, confinement, fetter, shackle, trammel, ceiling, glass ceiling, cap. let, knot, knag†, hitch, contretemps, screw loose, grit in the oil. prevention, preclusion, obstruction, stricture, restraint &c H0712, interclusion†, impedition†, retardment†, oppilation†. deterrent, hamper, roadblock, blockage.
Verbs: limit, restrict, confine, bar, check, hinder, constrain, restrain, hem in, cramp, curb, fetter, trammel. retard, preclude, inhibit &c H0778, shackle &c H0712, antevert†, countercheck†. hold back, hold in check, keep within bounds. impede, obstruct, impedite†.
Adjective: limited, restricted, confined, hemmed in, cramped, constrained.
Adverbs: within limits.
Foreign: German: Schranke.
Phrases: the frog at the bottom of the well, jing di zhi wa [Chin.] [Zhuangzi].
Hegel definition: Restriction is the limit of something posited as its own negative, a negative that is nonetheless essential to it. A bare limit lies quietly beside the existence of something; it becomes a restriction only when something transcends it in itself, referring to it from within as to something non-existent. Restriction is not anything alien or external to the finite: the finite's own determination is at the same time its restriction, and restriction is both itself and the ought, that in which the two are identical.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Existence › Finitude › Finitude › Restriction and the ought
Hegel citations:
In order for the limit that is in every something to be a restriction, the something must at the same time transcend it in itself – must refer to it from within as to a non-existent.
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › Restriction and the ought (tr. di Giovanni)
The restriction of the finite is not anything external, but the finite’s own determination is rather also its restriction; and this restriction is both itself and the ought; it is that which is common to both, or rather that in which the two are identical.
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › Restriction and the ought (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: The Ought
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › iii. Finitude as Such › 2. Restriction and the Ought › b. The Ought
Gloss: What something is to be but is not yet: the demand to go beyond its own restriction.
Hegelian gloss: Das Sollen, the in-itself of something set against its restriction, which it is to transcend and yet keeps as its limit.
Nouns: the ought. ought, oughtness, obligation, demand, requirement, imperative, exigency, norm, standard, ideal &c H0849, aspiration, striving, yearning, longing, the gap between is and ought, is-ought gap, vocation, task, mission, calling, deontology, deontic.
Verbs: strive, aspire, yearn, long, reach for, reach beyond, ought, should, must, be obliged, be bound, be called upon, transgress, overstep, exceed, surpass, push the envelope.
Adjective: obligatory, binding, incumbent, mandatory, imperative, normative, deontic, prescriptive, aspiring, striving, yearning, unfulfilled, unrealized, ideal. incumbent on, under obligation, bound by.
Adverbs: as it ought to be, as it should be, by rights, in principle, ideally, as it ought.
Phrases: du kannst, denn du sollst [Ger.] [Schiller, on Kant]; a man's reach should exceed his grasp, or what's a heaven for? [Browning]; ought implies can; ultra posse nemo obligatur [Lat.].
Hegel definition: The ought is the in-itself of something in its negative reference to its own limit, now posited as restriction. It is a determination that has a being-in-itself over against negation, and at the same time a non-being that is distinct from that determination. What ought to be is and is not: if it were, it would not merely ought to be. The ought therefore has a restriction essentially, and the finite as ought transcends its restriction while remaining bound to it.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Existence › Finitude › Finitude › Restriction and the ought
Hegel citations:
This in-itself, consequently, as negative reference to its limit (which is also distinguished from it), as negative reference to itself as restriction, is the ought.
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › Restriction and the ought (tr. di Giovanni)
What ought to be is, and at the same time is not. If it were, it would not be what merely ought to be. The ought has therefore a restriction essentially.
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › Restriction and the ought (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Transition of the Finite into the Infinite
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › b. Finitude › iii. Finitude as Such › 3. Transition of the Finite into the Infinite
Gloss: The way a limited thing, by pushing against its limit, goes beyond itself and points toward what has no limit.
Hegelian gloss: The finite, by sublating its own restriction, goes beyond itself and in this going-beyond is the infinite.
Nouns: transition of the finite into the infinite; self-transcendence, self-overcoming, self-surpassing; transgression, overstepping, overstepping of bounds, going beyond, exceeding, excess; elevation, ascent, ascension, uplift, exaltation, sublimation, rise; transcendence, transcendency, surpassing; apotheosis, deification; liberation; breakthrough, breakout, crossing, passage. the passage of the finite into the infinite, going beyond the limit, the self-sublation of the finite. jailbreak.
Verbs: transcend, surpass, exceed, overstep, overpass, outrun, outgrow, go beyond, get beyond, rise above, rise beyond, break through, break out, cross over; self-transcend, overcome oneself; elevate, exalt, sublimate; point beyond, outstep†. overreach, overleap, overgo†, overjump†, overskip†. transgress. transcend itself, pass over.
Adjective: self-transcending, self-surpassing, transcendent, transcending, liminal, transitional, transgressive; aspiring, upward, ascending, anagogic, anagogical. passing.
Adverbs: beyond, over and above, past; upward, onward, higher. beyond itself, into the infinite.
Foreign: German: Selbstüberwindung; Latin: excelsior; Greek: anabasis, epektasis [stretching forward], theōsis; Arabic: fanāʾ; Sanskrit: mokṣa [release], nirvāṇa.
Phrases: excelsior [Lat.]; man is something that shall be overcome [Nietzsche]; per aspera ad astra [Lat.]; plus ultra [Lat.]; beyond the pale; to go beyond.
Hegel definition: The transition of the finite into the infinite follows from the mutual connection of restriction and the ought, each of which contains the other. The finite is thus in itself the contradiction of itself: it sublates itself and ceases to be. At first it only becomes another finite, and so on to infinity. But in this ceasing to be, in the negation of itself, the finite has attained its being-in-itself: the ought, in going beyond restriction, and restriction, in pointing beyond itself, each rejoins itself. This identity with itself, negation of negation, is affirmative being, the other of the finite, which is the infinite.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Existence › Finitude › Finitude › Transition of the finite into the infinite
Hegel citations:
The finite is thus in itself the contradiction of itself; it sublates itself, it goes away and ceases to be.
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › Transition of the finite into the infinite, Remark (tr. di Giovanni)
[I]n its going-away and ceasing-to-be, in this negation of itself, the finite has attained its being-in-itself; in it, it has rejoined itself.
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › Transition of the finite into the infinite, Remark (tr. di Giovanni)
This identity with itself, the negation of negation, is affirmative being, is thus the other of the finite which is supposed to have the first negation for its determinateness; this other is the infinite.
— The Science of Logic, Finitude › Transition of the finite into the infinite, Remark (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Infinity
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › c. Infinity
Gloss: That which is not limited by anything outside it; boundlessness.
Hegelian gloss: The negation of the negation: the finite's own going-beyond itself, which first appears as the infinite set over against it.
Nouns: infinity, infinitude, the infinite; boundlessness, limitlessness, endlessness, illimitability, immeasurability, immensity, vastness, unboundedness, eternity &c; the unbounded, the unlimited, the endless; absolute, perfection, plenitude. infiniteness, perpetuity &c H0232. infinity &c H0063. unlimitedness.
Verbs: be infinite, have no limit, know no bounds, be without end, stretch to infinity, extend indefinitely. know no limits, have no limits, have no bounds, go on for ever. transcend, exceed all bounds.
Adjective: infinite, boundless, limitless, endless, unbounded, unlimited, illimitable, immeasurable, measureless, incalculable, innumerable, numberless, countless, inexhaustible, interminable, unending, never-ending, everlasting, eternal, perpetual; vast, immense, unfathomable, fathomless, bottomless; absolute, unconditioned, bathycolpian†, benthal†, benthopelagic†, downreaching†. uncircumscribed, boundless &c H0063. inconceivable, inconceptible†, searchless†.
Adverbs: infinitely, endlessly &c adj.; world without end, without limit, without end. boundlessly.
Foreign: German: das Unendliche; Latin: infinitum, ad infinitum, in infinitum, ens infinitum [Duns Scotus]; Greek: apeiron, plērōma; Hebrew: Ein Sof [the Endless]; Sanskrit: ananta [endless]; Chinese: wuji [limitless].
Phrases: to see a world in a grain of sand ... and eternity in an hour [Blake]; the eternal silence of these infinite spaces terrifies me [Pascal]; in my end is my beginning [T. S. Eliot]; to infinity and beyond.
Hegel definition: The infinite is the negation of negation, being that has reinstated itself out of restrictedness, and so may be taken as a new definition of the absolute. But by merely negating the finite it is not yet free of finitude. The true concept of infinity, the infinite of reason, must be distinguished from the bad infinity of the understanding, which in wanting to keep the infinite pure of the finite only makes it finite. The infinite is first simply the affirmative, then alternates with the finite, and is finally the self-sublation of both in one process.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Existence › Infinity
Hegel citations:
But, in fact, by just this negation the infinite is not already free from restrictedness and finitude. It is essential to distinguish the true concept of infinity from bad infinity, the infinite of reason from the infinite of the understanding. The latter is in fact a finitized infinite, and, as we shall now discover, in wanting to maintain the infinite pure and distant from the finite, the infinite is by that very fact only made finite.
— The Science of Logic, Existence › Infinity (tr. di Giovanni)
The infinite (a) in simple determination, is the affirmative as negation of the finite; (b) but is thereby in alternating determination with the infinite, and is abstract, one-sided infinite; (c) is the self-sublation of this infinite and of the finite in one process. This is the true infinite.
— The Science of Logic, Existence › Infinity (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: The Infinite in General
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › c. Infinity › i. The Infinite in General
Gloss: The unlimited in its first, simple sense: what the limited passes into when it goes beyond itself; the negation of the finite, taken as what truly is.
Hegelian gloss: The infinite in its simple concept: the affirmation that results as the negation of the finite.
Nouns: the infinite in general; the beyond, beyondness, transcendence, the transcendent, the other world, otherworldliness, the hereafter, yonder, the great beyond; the unconditioned, the absolute other, the wholly other; the not-finite, the nonfinite, negation of the finite; empyrean, heaven, the heavens; ideal, the ideal; true being. the infinite as such, the unlimited, the non-finite. boundlessness, endlessness, interminability, agelessness†.
Verbs: lie beyond, transcend, surpass, be other than, stand beyond, tower above. exceed, overpass. negate the finite.
Adjective: infinite, transcendent, transcendental, otherworldly, supramundane, supernal, celestial, ultramundane, beyond; unconditioned, absolute, ultimate; negative, apophatic. distant, remote, ulterior, transmarine†, transpontine†, unapproached†, incontiguous†. unearthly. unlimited.
Adverbs: beyond, in the beyond, yonder, over yonder, hereafter, in the hereafter; out of this world. far off, afar. without limit.
Foreign: German: das Jenseits, das ganz Andere; Arabic: al-ghayb [the unseen]; Sanskrit: paramārtha [ultimate]; Latin: aeternitas [the whole, simultaneous and perfect possession of boundless life] [Boethius].
Phrases: beyond the beyond; my kingdom is not of this world [Bible]; the undiscovered country from whose bourn no traveller returns [Hamlet]; without end; the sky's the limit.
Hegel definition: The infinite in general is the simple concept of the infinite: the negation of negation, the affirmative, being reinstated out of restrictedness. It is in a more intense sense than immediate being; it is true being, elevation above restriction, in which spirit is at home. It does not stand fixed above the finite, for it arises out of the finite's own nature, which is to refer to itself as restriction, to pass beyond it and so to become infinite. The finite has thus vanished into it, and what is, is only the infinite.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Existence › Infinity › The infinite in general
Hegel citations:
The infinite is the negation of negation, the affirmative, being that has reinstated itself out of restrictedness. The infinite is, in a more intense sense than the first immediate being; it is the true being; the elevation above restriction.
— The Science of Logic, Infinity › The infinite in general (tr. di Giovanni)
At the mention of the infinite, soul and spirit light up, for in the infinite the spirit is at home, and not only abstractly; rather, it rises to itself, to the light of its thinking, its universality, its freedom.
— The Science of Logic, Infinity › The infinite in general (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Alternating Determination of the Finite and the Infinite
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › c. Infinity › ii. Alternating Determination of the Finite and the Infinite
Gloss: The unlimited held apart from the limited, which makes it limited in turn; an endless alternation between the two, like a series that never arrives. Also called the bad or spurious infinite.
Hegelian gloss: The spurious (bad) infinite, fixed beyond the finite and so itself finite: the endless alternation of finite and infinite, the infinite progress.
Nouns: alternating determination of the finite and the infinite; bad infinity, spurious infinity; endless progression, infinite progress, infinite regress, regress, endless regress; perpetual ought, endless striving; vicious circle, merry-go-round, treadmill, rat race, squirrel cage, Sisyphean labour; Sisyphus, the stone of Sisyphus, Tantalus, the Danaids' sieve; tedium, monotony, repetition, iteration, sameness, ad nauseam; asymptote, horizon, mirage, receding goal, will-o'-the-wisp; turtles all the way down. recurrence, succession. the bad infinite, the spurious infinite, the endless progress, the alternation, the ought.
Verbs: alternate, oscillate, seesaw, shuttle, ping-pong, go back and forth, swing to and fro, see-saw; regress, recede; repeat, reiterate, iterate; go on forever, go round in circles, chase one's tail, run in place, tread water; never arrive. fluctuate, waver, vacillate, turn and turn about, wamble†. go on endlessly.
Adjective: endless, unending, interminable, never-ending, perpetual, ceaseless, incessant, sempiternal; repetitive, iterative, monotonous, tedious, Sisyphean, Tantalean; asymptotic, receding; alternating, oscillating, oscillatory, reciprocating; spurious, false, bad, vicious, pulsatory†, vibratile†. recursive [Comp.]. tiresome, insistent.
Adverbs: without end, on and on, again and again, over and over, round and round, back and forth, to and fro, hither and thither; et cetera, and so on, and so forth, and so on and so forth. backwards and forwards, wibble-wabble†. alternately. repeatedly, ofttimes†, unseldom†, not unfrequently†.
Foreign: German: schlechte Unendlichkeit, Wechselbestimmung; Latin: progressus in infinitum, regressus in infinitum, circulus vitiosus, ignis fatuus, ad infinitum, ad nauseam; Arabic: tasalsul [infinite chain]; Sanskrit: saṃsāra [cycle of rebirth], anavasthā [infinite regress]; Korean: angmuhan [bad infinite].
Phrases: turtles all the way down; great fleas have little fleas upon their backs to bite 'em [Augustus De Morgan]; who will guard the guards themselves? quis custodiet ipsos custodes? [Lat.] [Juvenal]; the more things change, the more they stay the same; an endless round.
Hegel definition: Taken immediately, as the non-being of an other, the infinite falls back into something determinate standing over against the finite. This is the bad infinite of the understanding, a beyond, empty and unattainable, which is limited by the finite and so itself finite. Each posits the other outside itself and each emerges only in the other. Their alternating determination runs on as the infinite progress: a limit is crossed, a new one arises, and so without end. It is the perpetual ought, a contradiction never resolved but only pronounced.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Existence › Infinity › Alternating determination of finite and infinite
Hegel citations:
As thus posited over against the finite, the two connected by the qualitative mutual reference of others, the infinite is to be called the bad infinite, the infinite of the understanding, for which it counts as the highest, the absolute truth.
— The Science of Logic, Infinity › Alternating determination of finite and infinite (tr. di Giovanni)
This bad infinite is in itself the same as the perpetual ought; it is indeed the negation of the finite, but in truth it is unable to free itself from it; the finite constantly resurfaces in it as its other, since this infinite only is with reference to the finite, which is its other. The progress to infinity is therefore only repetitious monotony, the one and the same tedious alternation of this finite and infinite.
— The Science of Logic, Infinity › Alternating determination of finite and infinite (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Affirmative Infinity
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › β. Determinate Being › c. Infinity › iii. Affirmative Infinity
Gloss: The unlimited understood as including the limited rather than lying beyond it; completeness rather than endlessness. Pictured as a circle, as against an endless line.
Hegelian gloss: True infinity, which contains the finite as a moment within itself: being returned to itself, imaged by the circle rather than the endless line.
Nouns: affirmative infinity, true infinity, genuine infinite; actual infinite, completed infinite; circle, cycle, ring, orb, sphere, round, closed curve, serpent swallowing its tail; return, homecoming, self-return; wholeness, totality, completeness, entirety, fullness, plenitude, perfection, consummation; self-containment, self-sufficiency, autarky; the whole; mandala; eternity, eternal now. integrity, unity &c H0038, completeness &c H0130, integration. hoop, annulus, loop, wheel, orbit, roundlet†, annulet†, contrate wheel†. circuit. fullness &c H0130. the true infinite, the affirmative infinite.
Verbs: return, come round, come full circle, close the circle, round off, complete, consummate, perfect; include, embrace, encompass, comprehend, contain. comprise. include &c H0154. enclose, encircle. return into itself.
Adjective: infinite, true, genuine, actual; circular, cyclic, cyclical, orbicular, spherical, rounded, self-returning, self-enclosed, self-contained, self-sufficient; whole, entire, complete, total, integral, perfect, consummate; all-embracing, all-encompassing, comprehensive, cycloidal†. annular. complete &c H0130. whole &c H0130, perfect &c H0207, absolute, plenary. truly infinite.
Adverbs: in full, all in all, altogether, through and through; full circle. truly, completely.
Foreign: German: wahrhafte Unendlichkeit, Rückkehr in sich, das Ganze; Latin: infinitum actu, nunc stans, in toto; Greek: ouroboros, plērōma; Sanskrit: maṇḍala; Chinese: taiji; Japanese: ensō [Zen circle]; Korean: chamdoen muhan [true infinite].
Phrases: in my end is my beginning [T. S. Eliot]; das Wahre ist das Ganze [Ger.] [Hegel]; God is an infinite sphere whose centre is everywhere and circumference nowhere [Liber XXIV philosophorum]; the circle closes.
Hegel definition: Affirmative or true infinity is the process in which the finite and the infinite are each only moments, each returning to itself through its negation. The finite sublates itself, and its infinity consists in this; the infinite is the transcending of the finite and contains it essentially. Neither is taken as a fixed unit, and their unity is not a motionless sameness but a becoming. It is not a beyond but is there, present, with determinateness in it. Its image is not the straight line that runs on but the circle, closed and wholly present, without beginning or end.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Existence › Infinity › Affirmative infinity
Hegel citations:
Thus the finite and the infinite are both this movement of each returning to itself through its negation; they are only as implicit mediation, and the affirmative of each contains the negative of each, and is the negation of the negation.
— The Science of Logic, Infinity › Affirmative infinity (tr. di Giovanni)
The image of the progression in infinity is the straight line; the infinite is only at the two limits of this line, and always only is where the latter (which is existence) is not but transcends itself, in its non-existence, that is, in the indeterminate. As true infinite, bent back upon itself, its image becomes the circle, the line that has reached itself, closed and wholly present, without beginning and end.
— The Science of Logic, Infinity › Affirmative infinity (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Being-for-Self
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › γ. Being-for-Self
Gloss: Self-containedness; the condition of a thing that relates only to itself, holding whatever is other within itself as an aspect of its own; independence.
Hegelian gloss: Being that has sublated all relation to other into relation to itself; infinite being turned back into itself; the truth of quality.
Nouns: being-for-self, being for itself; self-relation, self-reference, self-relatedness, reflexivity; independence, self-sufficiency, self-subsistence, self-containment, autonomy, autarky, aseity; individuality, selfhood, ipseity; completeness, wholeness, integrity, closure; ideality; being-in-and-for-itself. totality, entirety, unity &c H0038. self-containedness, being-for-itself, the for-itself.
Verbs: be for oneself, be by oneself, stand alone, stand on one's own feet, be self-sufficient, be one's own master; relate to oneself, refer to oneself; return into oneself, withdraw into oneself. be for itself, relate to itself.
Adjective: self-relating, self-referential, reflexive, self-contained, self-sufficient, self-subsistent, self-standing, self-reliant, independent, autonomous, autarkic, autarkical, sovereign; individual, singular; complete, whole, closed, rounded; ideal, operculated†. integral. entire, undivided. for-itself.
Adverbs: for itself; by itself, of itself, in its own right; on one's own, on one's own account. independently.
Foreign: German: Idealität, An-und-für-sich-sein, für sich; Latin: aseitas, ipseitas, sui juris; Greek: autarkeia; French: pour-soi, pour soi; Arabic: nafs [self]; Sanskrit: svātantrya [self-dependence], svabhāva [own-being]; Chinese: ziran [self-so, spontaneity]; Korean: daejajonjae [being-for-self].
Phrases: sui generis [Lat.]; to thine own self be true [Hamlet]; ipse dixit [Lat.]; in a world of one's own.
Hegel definition: Being-for-itself is qualitative being brought to completion, infinite being. In it the difference between being and determinateness, or negation, is posited and equalized, so that negation is simple self-reference. Something is for itself in so far as it sublates otherness and its connection with an other, having them in it only as sublated moments; it is the infinite turned back into itself. It is first immediately an existent for itself, the one; then the one passes into many ones through repulsion and attraction, and quality passes over into quantity.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Being-for-itself
Hegel citations:
In being-for-itself, qualitative being is brought to completion; it is infinite being
— The Science of Logic, Being-for-itself (tr. di Giovanni)
We say that something is for itself inasmuch as it sublates otherness, sublates its connection and community with other, has rejected them by abstracting from them. The other is in it only as something sublated, as its moment; being-for-itself consists in having thus transcended limitation, its otherness; it consists in being, as this negation, the infinite turning back into itself.
— The Science of Logic, Being-for-itself (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Being-for-Self as Such
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › γ. Being-for-Self › a. Being-for-Self as Such
Gloss: Self-relation as such: a thing complete in itself, no longer defined by its dealings with something else.
Hegelian gloss: Being-for-self taken simply, as the self-relation that has otherness only as sublated within it.
Nouns: being-for-self as such; pure self-relation, simple self-reference; returned-into-self, closure, self-enclosure, insularity; ideality of the finite; independence &c H0034; infinite self-relation; sufficiency, completeness. being-for-self in general, self-relation, the infinite return into self, the for-itself. ipseity.
Verbs: return into oneself, close upon oneself, be complete in oneself, need nothing else. relate to itself, be for itself, return into itself.
Adjective: self-enclosed, self-sufficient, self-complete, complete in itself, needing nothing, insular, closed, sealed, hermetic, archipelagic†. self-related, self-contained, complete.
Adverbs: as such, in and for itself. for itself, in itself complete.
Foreign: German: an und für sich; Latin: in se, per se.
Phrases: omnia mea mecum porto [Lat.] [Bias, via Cicero]; no man is an island [Donne] [Opposed]; by itself; on one's own account.
Hegel definition: Being-for-itself as such is being-for-itself taken in its general concept. Something is for itself in so far as it has transcended its limitation, rejecting its connection with an other and holding that other in it only as a moment. It relates to the limiting other polemically, and through negating it is reflected into itself. Consciousness already contains this determination but remains dual, since it still faces an external object; self-consciousness is being-for-itself brought to completion, the nearest example of infinity present, though of an abstract infinity.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Being-for-itself › Being-for-itself as such
Hegel citations:
Being-for-itself is the polemical, negative relating to the limiting other and, through this negation of the other, is being-reflected-within-itself
— The Science of Logic, Being-for-itself › Being-for-itself as such (tr. di Giovanni)
Self-consciousness, on the contrary, is being-for-itself brought to completion and posited; the side of reference to another, to an external object, is removed.
— The Science of Logic, Being-for-itself › Being-for-itself as such (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Determinate Being and Being-for-Self
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › γ. Being-for-Self › a. Being-for-Self as Such › i. Determinate Being and Being-for-Self
Gloss: Being there in relation to others, now kept only as an aspect within being complete in oneself.
Hegelian gloss: Determinate being preserved in being-for-self only as an ideal moment: being-for-other become being-for-one.
Nouns: determinate being and being-for-self; being-for-other and being-for-self; outwardness and inwardness; relatedness and independence; exposure and self-possession; presence to others and presence to self; public and private, extrinsic and intrinsic; heteronomy and autonomy. being-there and being-for-self, the contrast of determinate being and being-for-self, relation to other and self-relation. relativity.
Verbs: be there for others, be outward; withdraw, retire into oneself, keep to oneself; relate, connect. relate to other, relate to self, contrast.
Adjective: outward, exposed, relational, heteronomous; inward, self-possessed, self-collected, autonomous, expugnable†. determinate, self-related, other-related.
Adverbs: for others, for oneself; outwardly and inwardly; on the one hand, on the other, mauger†. for itself, for another.
Foreign: Korean: daetajonjae [being-for-other].
Phrases: neither a borrower nor a lender be [Hamlet]; for one; in another's eyes.
Hegel definition: Existence is preserved in being-for-itself, but only as a moment. Being-for-itself is infinity that has sunk into simple being, so that negation of negation is present in it only as infinite qualitative determinateness. Since being is still distinguished from that determinateness, existence belongs to it, for being-for-itself contains being affected by negation. The determinateness which in existence was an other, and a being-for-other, is bent back into the infinite unity of being-for-itself, and there existence is present as being-for-one.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Being-for-itself › Being-for-itself as such › Existence and being-for-itself
Hegel citations:
[B]eing-for-itself is infinity that has sunk into simple being; it is existence in so far as in the now posited form of the immediacy of being the negative nature of infinity, which is the negation of negation, is only as negation in general, as infinite qualitative determinateness.
— The Science of Logic, Being-for-itself as such › Existence and being-for-itself (tr. di Giovanni)
So the determinateness which in existence as such is an other, and a being-for-other, is bent back into the infinite unity of being-for-itself, and the moment of existence is present in the being-for-itself as being-for-one.
— The Science of Logic, Being-for-itself as such › Existence and being-for-itself (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Being-for-One
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › γ. Being-for-Self › a. Being-for-Self as Such › ii. Being-for-One
Gloss: The standing of whatever falls within a self-contained thing: it is there only as an aspect for that thing, not as an independent other; ideality.
Hegelian gloss: The ideality of the finite: what is in being-for-self has no being of its own, but is only for the one.
Nouns: being-for-one; ideality; for-me-ness, mineness; perspective, point of view, standpoint, angle, aspect, vantage point, viewpoint; representation, appearance-for, phenomenality; subjectivity, the subjective; appropriation, ownership, assimilation, taking-in; mental presence, intentional inexistence; the other as ideal moment. phase, light. the ideal moment, the moment, what is only for another. ideatum.
Verbs: be for one, be for someone, appear to, present itself to, count for, matter to; appropriate, assimilate, internalize, take in, make one's own. be ideal, be held as a moment.
Adjective: ideal, subjective, perspectival, apparent, phenomenal, internal, internalized, appropriated, assimilated, owned; for-me, mine. for-one, sublated.
Adverbs: for me, to me, in my view, in my eyes, from my standpoint; ideally, in idea. for one.
Foreign: German: Idealität, Jemeinigkeit; Latin: me judice; Sanskrit: sākṣin [witness].
Phrases: man is the measure of all things [Protagoras]; beauty is in the eye of the beholder; all in the mind.
Hegel definition: Being-for-one expresses how the finite is in its unity with the infinite, as idealized. In being-for-itself negation is no limit and refers to no other existence, so that although something is called being-for-one there is nothing other for which it could be. That for which it is and that which is for it are not yet distinct: what is for-one refers in its other only to itself. Thus the I, spirit, or God are idealizations because they are infinite, and God is for himself in so far as he is himself that which is for him.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Being-for-itself › Being-for-itself as such › Being-for-one
Hegel citations:
This moment gives expression to how the finite is in its unity with the infinite or as an idealization.
— The Science of Logic, Being-for-itself as such › Being-for-one (tr. di Giovanni)
An idealization is necessarily for-one, but it is not for an other; the one, for which it is, is only itself.
— The Science of Logic, Being-for-itself as such › Being-for-one (tr. di Giovanni)
God is therefore for himself, in so far he is himself that which is for him.
— The Science of Logic, Being-for-itself as such › Being-for-one (tr. di Giovanni)

Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › γ. Being-for-Self › a. Being-for-Self as Such › iii. The One
Gloss: A self-contained unit; the simplest notion of an individual that excludes everything else from itself.
Hegelian gloss: Being-for-self as immediate self-relation, excluding all other: the one, the principle of atomism.

Adjective: one, single, sole, only, lone, unique, singular, solitary, individual, unitary, monadic, atomic, indivisible, simple, uncompounded, undivided; exclusive. kithless†. unaccompanied, unattended, single-handed, odd, unrepeated†, azygous, first and last, isolated &c H0303, insular. insecable†, inseverable†, indiscerptible†, compact, irresolvable†. lonely, lonesome. monospermous†, unific†, uniflorous†, unifoliate†, unigenital†, uniliteral†, unijocular†, unimodular†.
