Phrases: e pluribus unum [Lat.]; hen kai pan [Gr.] [one and all]; ekam sat viprā bahudhā vadanti [Skt.] [Rigveda]; the One remains, the many change and pass [Shelley]; one and only; natura il fece [It.], e poi roppe la stampa [It.]; du fort au faible [Fr.]; two souls with but a single thought, two hearts that beat as one.
Hegel definition: The one is being-for-itself in the immediacy into which its moments have sunk: the simple unity of itself and its moments, an existent for itself. There is nothing in it but the self-reference of the sublating. Since in this immediacy its inner meaning vanishes, it is the totally abstract limit of itself. Because its moments appear outside one another while remaining inseparable, each determination of the one calls for its opposite, and this contradiction is what makes the exposition of the one difficult.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Being-for-itself › Being-for-itself as such › The one
Hegel citations:
Being-for-itself is the simple unity of itself and its moments, of the being for-one.
— The Science of Logic, Being-for-itself as such › The one (tr. di Giovanni)
Being-for-itself is thus an existent-for-itself, and, since in this immediacy its inner meaning vanishes, it is the totally abstract limit of itself – the one.
— The Science of Logic, Being-for-itself as such › The one (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: The One and the Many
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › γ. Being-for-Self › b. The One and the Many
Gloss: A unit seen in relation to other units like itself; unity and plurality.

Hegel definition: The one and the many is the development in which the one, the simple reference of being-for-itself to itself, shows that its immediacy cannot hold. The moments that had fallen together in it are now there as existents. As self-reference of the negative the one is a determining, and what is distinct from it is its own self-determining, demoted to reference. As negative unity it is therefore negation of itself as other, excluding the one from itself, so that the one passes into the void and into many ones.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Being-for-itself › The one and the many
Hegel citations:
The one is the simple reference of being-for-itself to itself in which its moments have fallen together – in which, therefore, being-for-itself has the form of immediacy and its moments, therefore, are now there as existents.
— The Science of Logic, Being-for-itself › The one and the many (tr. di Giovanni)
What shows itself to be present as distinct from the one is the one’s own self-determining; its unity with itself, as thus distinct from itself, is demoted to reference, and, as negative unity, it is negation of itself as other, the excluding of the one as an other from itself, from the one.
— The Science of Logic, Being-for-itself › The one and the many (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: The One in Its Own Self
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › γ. Being-for-Self › b. The One and the Many › i. The One in Its Own Self
Gloss: The unit considered by itself, simple and without internal division.
Hegelian gloss: The one as simple relation to itself, without any distinction within it.
Nouns: the one in its own self; simple unit, undivided unit, internal simplicity, inner unity, homogeneity, indivisibility, partlessness; atomicity, monadicity; the point, the simple; integrity, wholeness, intactness. unity &c H0038. the one by itself, the simple one, the unit in itself, the unalterable one. oneness, unicity.

Adjective: simple, undivided, indivisible, partless, uncompounded, unmixed, homogeneous, intact, whole, integral, atomic, monadic, internally unified, unmingled†. uniform, single, pure. elementary, undecomposed, unalloyed, untinged†, incomplex†. unbroken, unviolated†. insecable†, inseverable†, indiscerptible†, compact, irresolvable†. unalterable.

Hegel definition: The one in its own self simply is. Its being is not an existence or a determination through reference to an other, for it has negated that whole circle of categories, and so it cannot become any other: it is unalterable. Its indeterminateness is that of self-reference, absolutely determined being. Any direction from itself towards another is at once reversed. In it there is nothing, and this nothing, distinguished from its being, is posited as the void, the quality of the one in its immediacy.

Within it, the one just is; this, its being, is not an existence, not a determination as reference to an other, not a constitution; it is rather its having negated this circle of categories. The one is not capable, therefore, of becoming any other; it is unalterable.
— The Science of Logic, The one and the many › The one within (tr. di Giovanni)

— The Science of Logic, The one and the many › The one within (tr. di Giovanni)
The void is thus the quality of the one in its immediacy.
— The Science of Logic, The one and the many › The one within (tr. di Giovanni)

Phrases: nothing exists except atoms and empty space; everything else is opinion [Democritus]; natura abhorret vacuum [Lat.]; nature abhors a vacuum.
Hegel definition: The one and the void are the first existence of being-for-itself. The one is the void as the abstract self-reference of negation, yet the void, as nothing, is absolutely diverse from the affirmative being of the one, and so stands outside it. Because both stand in one reference to the one, their difference is posited, and in this opposition of the one and the void being-for-itself has again acquired an existence, while its unity withdraws to one side.

— The Science of Logic, The one and the many › The one and the void (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Plurality
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › γ. Being-for-Self › b. The One and the Many › iii. Plurality
Gloss: The rise of many units from one: in excluding others, a unit sets up others like itself, and plurality appears.

Verbs: repel; multiply, proliferate, pluralize, reproduce, replicate; scatter, disperse, fragment, atomize, split, splinter, divide, fission; self-divide. disseminate, diffuse, spread, distribute. push from, drive from &c H0242, chase, dispel, retrude†, abduce†, abduct, send away. diverge, divaricate, radiate, ramify, branch off, glance off, file off, fly off, fly off at a tangent, deviate &c H0238, part &c H0303.

Hegel definition: Plurality arises because the one, as negative reference to itself that is also reference to an existent, repels itself from itself and so is the becoming of many ones. The many are not produced for another and do not strictly come to be: each already is, referring only to itself, and repelled and repelling are alike. Their plurality is therefore not an otherness within them but a determination wholly external to the one. Their limit is the void, which neither joins them nor belongs to them. It is infinity as a self-producing contradiction.

This negative reference of the one to itself is repulsion.
— The Science of Logic, The one and the many › Many ones (tr. di Giovanni)

— The Science of Logic, The one and the many › Many ones (tr. di Giovanni)

— The Science of Logic, The one and the many › Many ones (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Repulsion and Attraction
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › γ. Being-for-Self › c. Repulsion and Attraction
Gloss: The two relations among many units: pushing apart, which keeps them separate, and drawing together, which unites them.
Hegelian gloss: Repulsion, through which the one posits the many, and attraction, through which the many are one; each presupposes the other.
Nouns: repulsion and attraction; push and pull, push-pull, centrifugal and centripetal force, expansion and contraction, systole and diastole; love and strife; concord and discord, harmony and strife; polarity, tension, equilibrium, balance; affinity and aversion, sympathy and antipathy. repulsion. attraction, pushing apart. repellence, attractivity.
Verbs: repel and attract, push and pull, drive away and draw together, expand and contract; balance, counterbalance, counterpoise, equilibrate. repel, drive apart, chase, retrude†, abduce†, abduct. draw together. attract, push apart.
Adjective: attractive and repulsive, centripetal and centrifugal, polar, bipolar, dynamic, tensile, magnetic. repellent, repulsive.
Adverbs: to and fro, back and forth, in and out; in tension, in balance. apart, together.
Foreign: German: Attraktion; Greek: philotēs kai neikos [Empedocles]; Sanskrit: rāga and dveṣa [attraction and aversion]; Chinese: yin and yang.
Phrases: love and strife [Empedocles]; opposites attract; birds of a feather flock together; like charges repel; opposite charges attract; like poles repel, opposite poles attract.
Hegel definition: Repulsion and attraction are the two ways in which the difference of the one and the many refers them to each other. Repulsion is the one's excluding of the many from itself; attraction is the self-positing of the many ones in a one. Each first appears on its own, outside the other, but neither can be had apart. Repulsion, though negative, is essentially connection, since what is fled from still stands in relation, so attraction is within repulsion itself; and attraction presupposes repulsion, which supplies its material. In their equilibrium quality passes over into quantity.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Being-for-itself › Repulsion and attraction
Hegel citations:
Although negative, repulsion is nonetheless essentially connection; the mutual repulsion and flight is not a liberation from what is repelled and fled from; that which is excluded still stands in connection with what is excluded from it. But this moment of connection is attraction, which is thus within repulsion itself
— The Science of Logic, Being-for-itself › Repulsion and attraction (tr. di Giovanni)
But it has been established that it is not just repulsion which is presupposed by attraction, but that there equally is present also a reverse connection of repulsion to attraction, and that repulsion no less has attraction for its presupposition.
— The Science of Logic, Being-for-itself › Repulsion and attraction (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Repulsion
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › γ. Being-for-Self › c. Repulsion and Attraction › i. Repulsion
Gloss: A unit's act of excluding others, which shows that its independence depends on the very others it excludes.
Hegelian gloss: Repulsion: the one's excluding of itself from itself into many ones, which as mutual exclusion proves their sameness (Ausschließen des Eins).
Nouns: repulsion; exclusion of the one; exclusion, shutting out, keeping out, ruling out, rejection, repudiation, ostracism, banishment, expulsion, exile, excommunication, ban, boycott, blackball, cold shoulder; exclusiveness, exclusivity, clannishness, cliquishness, insularity, isolationism, separatism; closure, enclosure, gatekeeping; uniqueness, singularity; mutual exclusion, mutually exclusive; nondependence; dependence of the excluder on the excluded. nonadmission, noninclusion†, preclusion, exception. separation, segregation, proscription. the excluding one, repulsion. apartness. repulsion, self-repulsion. driving from, repulse, abduction. magnetic repulsion, magnetic levitation, antigravity.
Verbs: exclude, shut out, keep out, rule out, bar, ban, debar, reject, repel, repudiate, ostracize, banish, expel, exile, excommunicate, blackball, boycott, blacklist, cold-shoulder, cut off, wall off, fence out; close ranks, disbench†. leave out, set apart, segregate, relegate. proscribe, keep at arm's length, send to Coventry, draw a cordon round. repulse, thrust away, push away, drive apart. push from, drive from &c H0242, dispel, send away. keep at arm's length, turn one's back upon, give the cold shoulder, send off, send away with a flea in one's ear.

[Young].
Hegel definition: Repulsion as exclusion is the relation of the many ones already present: each repels from itself the ones it has not generated. The repelling is mutual and from all sides, and it is how the many preserve themselves and distinguish themselves. But since in being ones they are all the same, and in negating one another they all do one and the same thing, this self-preservation proves to be their dissolution. They are only one affirmative unity, and the negative relating of the ones to one another is a coming together with oneself, which is attraction.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Being-for-itself › Repulsion and attraction › Exclusion of the one
Hegel citations:

— The Science of Logic, Repulsion and attraction › Exclusion of the one (tr. di Giovanni)
This self-preservation of the ones through their negative reference to one another is, however, rather their dissolution.
— The Science of Logic, Repulsion and attraction › Exclusion of the one (tr. di Giovanni)
The negative relating of the ones to one another is consequently only a coming-together-with-oneself.
— The Science of Logic, Repulsion and attraction › Exclusion of the one (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Attraction
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › γ. Being-for-Self › c. Repulsion and Attraction › ii. Attraction
Gloss: The single unity into which many units are drawn by attraction.

Hegel definition: The one one of attraction is the ideality toward which repulsion is only the ought, realized as the many ones pass over into one. Attraction presupposes repulsion, which supplies its material, and could not be completed without becoming an inert one that no longer attracts. It is the positing of a one distinct from the others, mediated through their negation. This one does not swallow the attracted ones abstractly into a point; containing repulsion in its determination, it keeps them as many within itself, so that in it repulsion and attraction are united.

The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Being-for-itself › Repulsion and attraction › The one one of attraction

Repulsion passes over into attraction, the many ones into one one.
— The Science of Logic, Repulsion and attraction › The one one of attraction (tr. di Giovanni)

— The Science of Logic, Repulsion and attraction › The one one of attraction (tr. di Giovanni)
It thus does not swallow the attracted ones within it as into one point, that is, does not sublate them abstractly.
— The Science of Logic, Repulsion and attraction › The one one of attraction (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: The Relation of Repulsion and Attraction
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › i. Determinateness (Quality) › γ. Being-for-Self › c. Repulsion and Attraction › iii. The Relation of Repulsion and Attraction
Gloss: The interplay of pushing apart and drawing together, each of which requires and passes into the other.
Hegelian gloss: Repulsion and attraction each the presupposition of the other, so that being-for-self passes over into quantity.
Nouns: relation of repulsion and attraction; equilibrium, balance, dynamic equilibrium, homeostasis, steady state, tension, polarity, reciprocity &c H0151; interplay, interaction, give and take, ebb and flow, systole and diastole; oscillation, pulsation, rhythm, breathing; dialectic of attraction and repulsion; ying and yang. the interplay of repulsion and attraction, mutual presupposition, the unity of repulsion and attraction, the passage into quantity.
Verbs: balance, counterbalance, equilibrate, offset, compensate; pulse, pulsate, oscillate, breathe; interact, interplay. counteract, countervail, counterpoise. presuppose, pass into each other.
Adjective: balanced, equilibrated, dynamic, reciprocal, mutual, interdependent, polar, rhythmic, pulsating. correlative.

Foreign: Latin: concordia discors, mutatis mutandis; Chinese: yin-yang.

Hegel definition: The relation of repulsion and attraction is that of two determinations which break out of the difference of the one and the many, each first appearing on its own and yet essentially joined with the other. Taken abstractly, repulsion would be the mere dispersion of the many; but even as negative it is connection, so attraction lies within it, and attraction in turn is only through repulsion. Each presupposes the other, and in the other relates to itself. Their unity is a becoming that collapses into simple immediacy, which is quantity.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Being-for-itself › Repulsion and attraction › The connection of repulsion and attraction
Hegel citations:
The difference of the one and the many has determined itself as a difference of their mutual reference connecting them which breaks down into two, repulsion and attraction, each of which stands at first outside the other on its own, in such a way that the two are essentially joined together nevertheless.
— The Science of Logic, Repulsion and attraction › The connection of repulsion and attraction (tr. di Giovanni)
In all this, however, the mediation of each with itself through the other is in fact negated; each of the two determinations is its own self-mediation.
— The Science of Logic, Repulsion and attraction › The connection of repulsion and attraction (tr. di Giovanni)
This being, according to the determination which it has now acquired, is quantity.
— The Science of Logic, Repulsion and attraction › The connection of repulsion and attraction (tr. di Giovanni)

Hegel definition: Pure quantity is quantity with as yet no determinateness or limit in it, a compact, infinite unity that continues itself into itself. Head: Continuous and Discrete Magnitude

Gloss: Quantity taken either as continuous, an unbroken whole like a line, or as discrete, a collection of separate units like a heap.

Posited in the determination of continuity, quantity is continuous magnitude; posited in the determinateness immanent to it, the one, it is discrete magnitude. Neither is a separate kind that falls outside the other.

Hegel definition: Extensive and intensive quantum are the two determinations of the quantitative limit itself. A quantum whose limit is a plurality is extensive magnitude; when that self-external plurality collapses into simple determinateness, it is intensive magnitude, or degree. Extensive magnitude has its amount within it, and degree has the amount outside it, but they are one and the same determinateness of quantum, each passing into the other. With this identity something qualitative comes on the scene, indifferent to the quantum it has.

Hegel definition: Intensive quantum, or degree, is quantum whose limit is simple and identical with it. The self-external plurality of extensive quantum has gathered itself into a single determination: degree is a determinate magnitude but not an aggregate. The twentieth degree is not a sum of twenty degrees; it is that one degree, in which number is present as a sublated amount. Its determinateness lies outside it, in its connection with other degrees, so that ascent and descent along the scale form a continuous flow.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Quantum › Extensive and intensive quantum
Hegel citations:
Degree is thus a determinate magnitude, a quantum, but at the same time it is not an aggregate or several within itself

When we speak of 10 or 20 degrees, the quantum which has that many degrees – the tenth, the twentieth
— The Science of Logic, Quantum › Extensive and intensive quantum (tr. di Giovanni)
This reference connecting a degree through itself to its other makes ascent and descent on the scale of degrees a continuous progress, a flow, which is an uninterrupted and indivisible alteration
— The Science of Logic, Quantum › Extensive and intensive quantum (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Identity of Extensive and Intensive Magnitude
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › ii. Magnitude › β. Quantum › b. Extensive and Intensive Quantum (Degree) › iii. Identity of Extensive and Intensive Magnitude
Gloss: The interchangeability of size and degree: an intensity can be read off as a length on a scale, and a size felt as an intensity.
Hegelian gloss: Each kind of magnitude passes into the other: degree is expressed in an outside many, and an extent is felt as one intensity.

Adjective: equivalent, interchangeable, convertible, correspondent, corresponding, commensurate, proportional; calibrated, graduated. tantamount. identical.
Adverbs: equivalently, correspondingly; in proportion, proportionally. interchangeably, as one.
Phrases: the higher the column, the hotter the day; as much as the other; the same difference.
Hegel definition: The identity of extensive and intensive magnitude is that they are one determinateness of quantum, distinguished only in that one has its amount within and the other without. Degree has its determinateness through its connection with an amount that is its own, and so is extensive; extensive magnitude collapses into the oneness of degree and steps outside it. With this identity there comes forth a something, mediated with itself through the negation of these distinct terms, which has a quantum while its qualitative existence is indifferent to it.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Quantum › Extensive and intensive quantum › Identity of extensive and intensive magnitude
Hegel citations:
Extensive magnitude passes over into intensive magnitude because its many collapses in and for itself into oneness and steps outside it. But, conversely, this simple one has its determinateness only in the amount, its amount; indifferent to the otherwise determined intensities, it has the externality of amount in it; thus intensive magnitude is just as essentially extensive magnitude.
— The Science of Logic, Extensive and intensive quantum › Identity of extensive and intensive magnitude (tr. di Giovanni)
With this identity, the qualitative something comes on the scene; for the identity is the unity that refers back to itself through the negation of its distinct terms
— The Science of Logic, Extensive and intensive quantum › Identity of extensive and intensive magnitude (tr. di Giovanni)

Hegel definition: Alteration belongs to quantum by its quality. A quantum is a determinateness posited as sublated, the contradiction of being simple self-reference and yet having its determinateness in another quantum. So it is continuous with its otherness, and not only can every determination of magnitude be passed beyond, it is posited that it must alter. Quantum repels itself from itself and sends itself beyond itself in increase and decrease, each new limit again sublating itself, and so on to infinity.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Quantum › Extensive and intensive quantum › Alteration of quantum
Hegel citations:
A quantum, according to its quality, is therefore in absolute continuity with its externality, with its otherness. Consequently, not only can every determinateness of magnitude be transcended, not only can it be altered: that it must alter is now posited.
— The Science of Logic, Extensive and intensive quantum › Alteration of quantum (tr. di Giovanni)
Thus quantum sends itself beyond itself; this other which it becomes is at first itself a quantum, but a quantum which is not a static limit but one that impels itself beyond itself. The limit which arises in this beyond is therefore only one that again sublates itself and sends itself to a further limit, and so on to infinity.
— The Science of Logic, Extensive and intensive quantum › Alteration of quantum (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Quantitative Infinity
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › ii. Magnitude › β. Quantum › c. Quantitative Infinity
Gloss: The endlessness built into quantity: any amount can always be exceeded.
Hegelian gloss: The quantum's self-contradiction: being a definite amount, it is always to be surpassed; the infinite progress.
Nouns: quantitative infinity; the infinitely great and the infinitely small, the infinitesimal, infinitesimals, infinitely small quantities, evanescent quantities, ghosts of departed quantities; the infinite in mathematics, mathematical infinite, transfinite, aleph, ∞, lemniscate; limit, limiting value, asymptote; calculus, infinitesimal calculus, differential calculus, integral calculus, method of exhaustion, fluxions; indefiniteness, unboundedness, endlessness. calculus of differences. computation, calculation. the quantitative infinite, boundlessness of amount, the infinitely great, the infinitely small.
Verbs: approach a limit, tend toward, converge, diverge; increase without bound, grow indefinitely, shrink indefinitely; differentiate, integrate. exceed, surpass, outgo. outperform.
Adjective: infinite, infinitesimal, transfinite, asymptotic, unbounded, indefinite, immeasurable, incalculable, limitless; convergent, divergent. immense, numberless, countless, sumless†, measureless, illimitable, inexhaustible, interminable, unfathomable, unapproachable, exhaustless, without number, without measure, without limit, without end, incomprehensible, endless, boundless, termless†, untold, unnumbered, unmeasured, unlimited, illimited†, perpetual, unexhausted†, unwasted†. converging, asymptotical. numerical, incommensurable, innumerable. exceedable.
Adverbs: infinitely, indefinitely, without bound, in the limit.
Foreign: Latin: ad infinitum.
Phrases: the ghosts of departed quantities [Berkeley]; to infinity and beyond; on and on.
Hegel definition: Quantitative infinity is the sphere in which quantum, determined in itself and yet outside itself, shows that finitude and infinity each contain the moment of the other. The finitude of quantum is its being limited and its sending itself beyond itself; its infinity is its unlimitedness and its being turned back into itself. Unlike the qualitative infinite, which stands abstractly opposed to the finite, here the finite continues into its beyond and refers to itself in it, first in the infinite progress.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Quantum › Quantitative infinity
Hegel citations:
In quantum, finitude and infinity (the latter supposedly separate from finitude, as bad infinity) each already possesses within it the moment of the other.
— The Science of Logic, Quantum › Quantitative infinity (tr. di Giovanni)
The qualitative and quantitative infinite are distinguished inasmuch as in the former the opposition of the finite and infinite is qualitative, and the transition of the finite into the infinite, or the reference of each to the other, is present only in the in-itself, in their concept.
— The Science of Logic, Quantum › Quantitative infinity (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Concept of Quantitative Infinity
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › ii. Magnitude › β. Quantum › c. Quantitative Infinity › i. Concept of Quantitative Infinity
Gloss: The idea that a quantity always points beyond itself to a larger or smaller one.
Hegelian gloss: The quantum's determination to be beyond itself, the infinite as its own other.
Nouns: concept of quantitative infinity; self-surpassing of quantum, self-transcendence of quantity, inherent beyond, built-in incompleteness; open-endedness, indefinite extensibility, potential infinite; the next number, successor, the always-more; insatiability, unquenchability. the beyond of quantum, the ought of quantity. infinitesimal, the transfinite.
Verbs: point beyond, outrun itself, exceed itself, go beyond itself, overreach; extend indefinitely. surpass itself, exceed.
Adjective: open-ended, indefinitely extensible, unfinished, incomplete, insatiable, unquenchable, self-surpassing, potential. exceeding, unbounded.
Adverbs: always more, ever more, beyond any given amount. beyond itself, further.
Foreign: Latin: infinitum potentia; Greek: apeiron.
Phrases: there is always a bigger fish; the sky's the limit; beyond measure; out of all proportion.
Hegel definition: The concept of quantitative infinity is that quantum's alteration into another quantum goes on without end because quantum is inherently self-contradictory. It becomes another yet continues in its otherness, so that the other is again a quantum, but the other of quantum as such, its own unlimitedness. Quantum is an ought: it implies being determined for itself, and this is rather being determined in an other. The sending beyond itself that makes it finite is equally the determination of the infinite.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Quantum › Quantitative infinity › Its concept
Hegel citations:
Quantum becomes an other; but it continues in its otherness; the other is therefore also a quantum. This latter, however, is the other, not of a quantum, but of the quantum as such, the negative of itself as a limited something, and hence its own unlimitedness, infinity.
— The Science of Logic, Quantitative infinity › Its concept (tr. di Giovanni)
Quantum is an ought; it implies that it be determined-for-itself, and this being-determined-for-itself is rather the being determined in an other
— The Science of Logic, Quantitative infinity › Its concept (tr. di Giovanni)

Hegel definition: The quantitative infinite progress expresses the contradiction in quantum without resolving it. Quantum has a beyond of itself to which it passes; since it is continuous with that beyond, the beyond is again a quantum, which flees beyond itself in turn. The progress is the task of reaching the infinite without reaching it, a perpetual generating of the infinite that never gets past quantum and never has the infinite positively present, though the continuity of the terms gives it the appearance of a resolution.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Quantum › Quantitative infinity › The quantitative infinite process
Hegel citations:
The infinite progress is now the expression of this contradiction, not the resolution of it; however, because of the continuity of one determinateness in the other, the progress gives rise to the semblance of a resolution in a union of the two.
— The Science of Logic, Quantitative infinity › The quantitative infinite process (tr. di Giovanni)
As at first posited, such a progress is the task of attaining the infinite but not the attainment of it; it is a perpetual generation of the infinite, without the progress of ever getting beyond the quantum itself, and without the infinite ever becoming something which is positively present.
— The Science of Logic, Quantitative infinity › The quantitative infinite process (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: The Infinity of Quantum
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › ii. Magnitude › β. Quantum › c. Quantitative Infinity › iii. The Infinity of Quantum
Gloss: The recognition that quantity's endless going-beyond is its own nature; quantity understood as wholly relational.
Hegelian gloss: The quantum known as essentially self-external, so that its truth lies in its relation to another quantum: the ratio.
Nouns: infinity of quantum; quantitative relation, ratio &c H0065; the infinite as a moment of quantity; the quality of quantity; relational magnitude; limit concept; derivative, differential quotient, dy/dx, rate of change; ratio of infinitesimals. the infinite quantum, the true quantitative infinite, quantity as relation, the qualitative moment of quantum, the return of quality. commensuration.
Verbs: relate, proportion, take the limit, differentiate. go beyond itself, return to itself.
Adjective: relational, proportional, differential, infinitesimal, limiting. integral. infinite, self-related.
Adverbs: in the limit, relatively, proportionally. infinitely, relationally.
Phrases: the infinitely small is not nothing; in proportion; out of proportion.
Hegel definition: The infinity of quantum is what the infinite progress contains when its moments are taken together. The infinitely great and infinitely small are insubstantial images, each at once a quantum and its non-being. In the progress quantum is sublated, and so is its beyond, and the truth is the unity of these two negations. Quantum is precisely through its externality itself, with itself in its negation, so that the progress posits the concept of quantum and restores magnitude as a limit that is indifferent or external, now with a qualitative character.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Quantum › Quantitative infinity › The infinity of quantum
Hegel citations:
The infinitely great and the infinitely small are, therefore, figurative representations which on closer inspection prove to be but unsubstantial nebulous shadows.
— The Science of Logic, Quantitative infinity › The infinity of quantum (tr. di Giovanni)
But this is what quantum as such is in itself. For through its externality it is precisely itself; the externality constitutes that in virtue of which quantum is quantum, where it is with itself. In the infinite progress, therefore, the concept of quantum is posited.
— The Science of Logic, Quantitative infinity › The infinity of quantum (tr. di Giovanni)
Its truth is the unity of these two negations in which the negations are, but as moments.
— The Science of Logic, Quantitative infinity › The infinity of quantum (tr. di Giovanni)

Hegel definition: Quantitative ratio is the infinite quantum as the unity of quantitative and qualitative determinateness. In ratio a quantum is no longer indifferently determined: it refers to its beyond, which is another quantum, and each has its determinateness in this reference, so that in the other it has returned into itself. The relation is itself a magnitude, a self-enclosed whole. It runs from direct ratio through inverse ratio to the ratio of powers, where the qualitative moment, fully posited, becomes measure.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Ratio or the quantitative relation
Hegel citations:
In ratio, quantum no longer has a merely indifferent determinateness but is qualitatively determined as simply referring to its beyond.
— The Science of Logic, Ratio or the quantitative relation (tr. di Giovanni)
It continues in its beyond, and this beyond is at first just an other quantum. Essentially, however, the two do not refer to each other as external quanta but each rather possesses its determinateness in this reference to the other. In this, in their otherness, they have thus returned into themselves; what each is, that it is in its other; the other constitutes the determinateness of each.
— The Science of Logic, Ratio or the quantitative relation (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Direct Ratio
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › ii. Magnitude › γ. Quantitative Ratio › a. Direct Ratio
Gloss: A relation in which two amounts rise or fall together, keeping a constant quotient; direct proportion.
Hegelian gloss: Ratio in which the exponent is a fixed quotient of two quanta that vary together.
Nouns: direct ratio; direct proportion, direct variation, linear relation, linearity, constant ratio, constant quotient, proportionality constant, rate, gradient, slope; correspondence, covariation, correlation, positive correlation; lockstep, parity, parallel. direct relation, the exponent.
Verbs: vary directly, keep pace with, increase together, correlate, track, follow, match, scale with, outmarch†. rise and fall together.
Adjective: directly proportional, proportionate, linear, corresponding, covariant, correlated, positively correlated, in lockstep. direct, proportional.
Adverbs: in direct proportion, proportionally, in step, in tandem, hand in hand. directly.
Foreign: Latin: pari passu.
Phrases: pari passu [Lat.]; the more, the more.
Hegel definition: Direct ratio is the immediate ratio, in which the determinateness of each quantum lies in that of the other. Both have only one limit, itself a quantum, the exponent. One side counts as unit and the other as amount, and when one is altered the other is increased or decreased in proportion, so that the two really make up only one quantum. Because the exponent, as a mere quotient, does not settle which side is unit and which amount, the direct ratio passes into the inverse ratio.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Ratio or the quantitative relation › The direct ratio
Hegel citations:
In the ratio which, as immediate, is direct, the determinateness of each quantum lies in the reciprocal determinateness of the other. There is only one determinateness or limit of both – one which is itself a quantum, namely the exponent of the ratio.
— The Science of Logic, Ratio or the quantitative relation › The direct ratio (tr. di Giovanni)
Accordingly, the two truly constitute only one quantum; the one side has only the value of unit with respect to the other, not of an amount; and the other only that of amount.
— The Science of Logic, Ratio or the quantitative relation › The direct ratio (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Inverse Ratio
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › ii. Magnitude › γ. Quantitative Ratio › b. Inverse Ratio
Gloss: A relation in which one amount rises as the other falls, keeping a constant product; inverse proportion.
Hegelian gloss: Ratio in which the product stays constant as one side grows and the other shrinks.
Nouns: inverse ratio; inverse proportion, inverse variation, reciprocal relation, reciprocity, constant product, trade-off, tradeoff, compensation, counterbalance, seesaw, zero-sum, negative correlation; hyperbola; the more the less. counterpoise, equivalent. reciprocal ratio, inverse relation. reciprocality.

Adjective: inversely proportional, inverse, reciprocal, compensatory, negatively correlated, zero-sum.
Adverbs: inversely, conversely, contrariwise, in inverse proportion, the more the less, hirdy-girdy†.
Foreign: Latin: vice versa.
Phrases: what one gains the other loses; robbing Peter to pay Paul.
Hegel definition: Inverse ratio is the direct ratio sublated: the exponent now has the value of a product, the unity of unit and amount, and the ratio itself has become alterable. As one side increases the other decreases, so that each is what it is by relating negatively to the other, while the exponent, a fixed quantum, is the limit of their reciprocal limiting, a beyond each approaches endlessly. Since the exponent preserves itself in the negation of every particular value of its moments, the ratio becomes the ratio of powers.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Ratio or the quantitative relation › The inverse ratio
Hegel citations:
The ratio as now before us is the sublated direct ratio.
— The Science of Logic, Ratio or the quantitative relation › The inverse ratio (tr. di Giovanni)
This consisted in the fact that the quantum is immediate but at the same time so connected to an other that the greater it is, the smaller is the other, that it is what it is by virtue of negatively relating to the other
— The Science of Logic, Ratio or the quantitative relation › The inverse ratio (tr. di Giovanni)
In the ratio now before us, the exponent as the determining quantum is thus posited as negative towards itself as a quantum of the ratio, and hence as qualitative, as limit
— The Science of Logic, Ratio or the quantitative relation › The inverse ratio (tr. di Giovanni)

Phrases: the rich get richer; doubling every year; squared and cubed; to the nth degree.
Hegel definition: The ratio of powers is the ratio in which quantum, self-identical in its otherness, determines its own passing beyond itself. The amount is determined only by the unit: it is the unit itself, so that a power is an aggregate of units each of which is that aggregate. The exponent is of a wholly qualitative nature. Here quantum fully realizes its concept; it has returned into itself and become quality again, and the truth of quantum is measure.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Ratio or the quantitative relation › The ratio of powers
Hegel citations:
This is the case in the ratio of powers where the unit, which in it is amount, is at the same time the amount as against itself as unit. The otherness, the amount of units, is the unit itself.
— The Science of Logic, Ratio or the quantitative relation › The ratio of powers (tr. di Giovanni)
The ratio of powers is the display of what the quantum is implicitly in itself; it expresses its determinateness of quantum or the quality by which it is distinguished from another.
— The Science of Logic, Ratio or the quantitative relation › The ratio of powers (tr. di Giovanni)
Quantum is henceforth no longer an indifferent or external determination but is sublated as such, and it is a quality and that by virtue of which anything is what it is; the truth of quantum is to be measure.
— The Science of Logic, Ratio or the quantitative relation › The ratio of powers (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Measure
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › iii. Measure
Gloss: An amount that is essential to what a thing is, so that beyond certain limits a change in amount becomes a change in kind; proportion, due size, standard.
Hegelian gloss: The unity of quality and quantity: the qualitative quantum, beyond whose limits a change of amount becomes a change of kind.
Nouns: measure; proportion, due proportion, right proportion, symmetry, harmony, balance, moderation, temperance, restraint, mean, the mean, golden mean, middle way; standard, norm, criterion, canon, rule, yardstick, benchmark, gauge, scale, measure of all things; due size, fitness, appropriateness, decorum, propriety, ratio; the specific quantity of a thing; balance of quality and quantity; mean between excess and defect. yard measure, foot rule, compass, calipers, gage, meter, line, rod, check, dividers, velo†. average, median, mode, medium, mediocrity, generality, compromise &c H0689, middle state, neutrality. middle course, midcourse, mean &c H0054, middle &c H0228. dueness &c H0683, seemliness. due measure. easing. mesotes, modicum. armillary sphere†.

Adjective: measured, proportionate, proportioned, balanced, harmonious, symmetrical, moderate, temperate, restrained, sober, sane, even, fitting, appropriate, due, apt, seemly, commensurate. reasonable, tempered. within compass.
Adverbs: in due measure, in moderation, within measure, within reason, in proportion; neither too much nor too little. in measure.
Foreign: Latin: mensura, modus, aurea mediocritas; Greek: metron, sōphrosynē, mesotēs [the mean], kairos [right time], ariston metron, mēden agan; French: juste milieu; Italian: mezzo termine; Arabic: wasaṭ [middle, moderation]; Sanskrit: madhyamā pratipad; Chinese: zhongyong [doctrine of the mean].

Hegel definition: Measure is the unity of quality and quantity. Being as such is determinateness immediately equal to itself; quantity is being returned to itself as indifferent to determinateness, having it only in an other. Measure is the third, externality referring to itself, which is thus sublated externality and carries its difference within it, the quantitative moment and the qualitative moment. It is the quantum on which the quality of a thing depends.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Measure
Hegel citations:
Abstractly expressed, quality and quantity are in measure united.
— The Science of Logic, Measure (tr. di Giovanni)
As third, we now have the externality that refers itself to itself; as self-reference, it is at the same time sublated externality and carries the difference from itself in it – a difference which, as externality, is the quantitative moment, and, as taken back into itself, the qualitative.
— The Science of Logic, Measure (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Specific Quantity
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › iii. Measure › α. Specific Quantity
Gloss: An amount that carries a quality, as a certain temperature is the boiling point of water.
Hegelian gloss: Measure as immediate: a quantum to which a quality is bound.
Nouns: specific quantity; critical point, threshold, tipping point, boiling point, freezing point, melting point, flash point, ignition point, breaking point, saturation point, dew point; specific heat, specific gravity &c H0267; constant, physical constant, characteristic value; critical mass, quorum. diagnostic, lineament, feature, trait. the qualitative quantity, quantity with a quality, the specific magnitude, the critical amount. modulus.
Verbs: reach a threshold, hit the critical point, tip over, tip. specify, qualify, carry a quality.
Adjective: critical, threshold, characteristic, specific, defining, decisive, pivotal. definite, determinate. qualitative.
Adverbs: at the critical point, at the threshold, on the cusp. specifically, at a certain amount.
Phrases: the last straw; made to measure; the measure of all things.
Hegel definition: Specific quantity is the first form of measure, qualitative quantity. It is first an immediate, specific quantum. Second, in relating to another it becomes a specifying of the indifferent quantum, a rule containing the two moments of measure as different, the quantitative determinateness and the external quantum. Third, these two sides themselves become qualities, and the rule becomes a relation of the two, one measure that specifies itself further into a difference of measures.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Measure › Specific quantity
Hegel citations:
Qualitative quantity is, first, an immediate, specific quantum; and this quantum, second, in relating itself to another, becomes a quantitative specifying, a sublating of the indifferent quantum.
— The Science of Logic, Measure › Specific quantity (tr. di Giovanni)
In this difference, however, the two sides become qualities, and the rule becomes a relation of the two
— The Science of Logic, Measure › Specific quantity (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: The Specific Quantum
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › iii. Measure › α. Specific Quantity › a. The Specific Quantum
Gloss: A definite amount bound up with a particular quality; the size at which a thing is what it is.
Hegelian gloss: A quantum that is the existence of a quality, so that the thing is what it is only within this amount.
Nouns: the specific quantum; proper amount, right size, due measure, natural size, characteristic magnitude; norm, optimum, just right, sweet spot; quota, allotment, dose; fitting proportion, appropriate scale, human scale. measure, quantum, ratio, proportion. the specific amount, the proper size, the qualitative quantum, the determinate size, the natural measure.
Verbs: fit, suit, befit; be the right size, be just right. specify, fix, be of a size.
Adjective: proper, appropriate, fitting, due, right-sized, optimal, characteristic, specific. definite, determinate.
Adverbs: just right, just so, to a nicety, to a T. at its proper size, specifically.
Phrases: Goldilocks's porridge: not too hot, not too cold; just so much; in due measure.
Hegel definition: The specific quantum is measure in its immediacy, quantum which as self-referring externality is itself quality: an immediate quantum with an immediate quality belonging to it. Whatever is has a measure, a magnitude that belongs to its nature, so that if it exceeds or falls short of it the thing perishes. The quantum can yet vary within limits without the quality changing, and so a thing can be taken unawares: a change that seems merely quantitative suddenly turns qualitative, as with the bald head and the heap.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Measure › Specific quantity › The specific quantum
Hegel citations:
Every existence has a magnitude, and this magnitude belongs to the very nature of a something; it constitutes its determinate nature and its in-itself. The something is not indifferent to this magnitude, as if, were the latter to alter, it would remain the same; rather the alteration of the magnitude alters its quality.
— The Science of Logic, Specific quantity › The specific quantum (tr. di Giovanni)
The ancients had already taken notice of this coincidence, that an alteration which appears to be only quantitative suddenly changes into a qualitative one
— The Science of Logic, Specific quantity › The specific quantum (tr. di Giovanni)
Quantum, when it is taken as indifferent limit, is the side from which an existence is unsuspectedly attacked and laid low.
— The Science of Logic, Specific quantity › The specific quantum (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Specifying Measure
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › iii. Measure › α. Specific Quantity › b. Specifying Measure
Gloss: Measure that applies its own standard to something else, fixing the amounts that belong to it.
Hegelian gloss: Measure as a standard that determines another quantum by itself.
Nouns: specifying measure; standard, rule, norm, criterion, gauge, yardstick, benchmark, touchstone, canon, model; regulation, calibration, standardization, normalization; specification, spec, tolerance. measure. regularity, formula, rule &c H0775. pattern. prototype. the measuring that specifies, the application of a standard, the rule and the specified.
Verbs: specify, standardize, calibrate, normalize, regulate, gauge, measure against. apply a standard, fix.
Adjective: standard, normative, regulative, regulatory, criterial, canonical. specifying, specificatory, determining.
Adverbs: by the book, according to the standard, to spec. specifically, by its own standard.
Foreign: German: das spezifizierende Maß.
Phrases: the measure of a man; to take the measure of; set the standard.
Hegel definition: Specifying measure is the measure of one thing acting on the indifferent, external quantum of another. It is first a rule, an arbitrary unit applied from outside, but as specific measure its nature is to relate to an other. A something with an inner measure does not simply take on an alteration of magnitude that comes from outside: it reacts against it, assimilates it in its own way and makes something else of it, showing itself to be for itself in this externality. Measure then exists as a ratio whose exponent is its specific character.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Measure › Specific quantity › Specifying measure
Hegel citations:
Measure is a specific determining of the external magnitude, that is, of the indifferent magnitude which is now posited in the measuring something by some other concrete existence in general.
— The Science of Logic, Specific quantity › Specifying measure (tr. di Giovanni)
Its measure reacts against it, behaves towards the aggregate as an intensive measure and assimilates it in a way typically its own; it alters the externally imposed alteration, makes something else out of this quantum and demonstrates through this specifying function that in this externality it is for-itself.
— The Science of Logic, Specific quantity › Specifying measure (tr. di Giovanni)

Hegel definition: The rule, or standard, is measure as it first specifies: a magnitude determinate in itself serving as a unit for a quantum belonging to some other concrete existence, which it measures by fixing it as an amount of that unit. The comparison is an external act, and the unit itself is an arbitrary magnitude which can in turn be treated as an amount, as a foot is an amount of inches. Yet measure is not only an external rule, for as specific measure it relates by its own nature to its other.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Measure › Specific quantity › Specifying measure › The rule
Hegel citations:
The rule, or the standard which we have just mentioned, is in the first instance as a magnitude which is determinate in itself and is a unit with respect to a quantum of a particular concrete existence: this is a quantum with a concrete existence which is other than the something of the rule – is measured by the latter, that is, is determined as the amount of the said unit.
— The Science of Logic, Specifying measure › The rule (tr. di Giovanni)
This comparison is an external act, and the unit itself is an arbitrary magnitude
— The Science of Logic, Specifying measure › The rule (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Specifying Measure Proper
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › iii. Measure › α. Specific Quantity › b. Specifying Measure › ii. Specifying Measure Proper
Gloss: Measure that modifies what it measures according to its own nature, as a body takes up heat according to its own capacity.
Hegelian gloss: Measure that takes up an external quantum and alters it according to its own nature, as a body takes up heat by its specific capacity.
Nouns: specifying measure proper; capacity, specific capacity, specific heat, heat capacity, absorption, uptake, receptivity, susceptibility, coefficient, modulus, factor, index; nonlinear response, specific response, refraction &c H0284; assimilation according to one's own nature. multiplier. the specifying measure in the strict sense, the modifying measure.

Adjective: specific, characteristic, idiosyncratic, receptive, absorptive, susceptible, modulating. specifying, modifying.
Adverbs: after its own fashion, after its kind, in its own way. specifically, according to its own nature.
Phrases: quidquid recipitur, ad modum recipientis recipitur [Lat.] [Aquinas]; according to its capacity.
Hegel definition: Specifying measure proper is the determining of an external, indifferent magnitude by the qualitative side of the measuring something. A something with its own inner measure receives an alteration of magnitude from outside, but does not take it on as an arithmetical sum: it reacts against it as an intensive measure, assimilates it in its own manner and turns it into something else. The specified amount still varies with the external one, but in a constant way, so that measure exists as a ratio whose exponent expresses its specific character.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Measure › Specific quantity › Specifying measure › Specifying measure
Hegel citations:
Inasmuch as a something has an internal measure, an alteration of the magnitude of its quality comes to it from outside, and the something does not take on the arithmetical aggregate of the alteration.
— The Science of Logic, Specifying measure › Specifying measure (tr. di Giovanni)
The specified aggregate is therefore also alterable, but is not for that reason a quantum as such but the external quantum as specified in a constant manner.
— The Science of Logic, Specifying measure › Specifying measure (tr. di Giovanni)
Measure thus has its determinate existence as a ratio, and its specificity is in general the exponent of this ratio.
— The Science of Logic, Specifying measure › Specifying measure (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Relation of the Two Sides as Qualities
Head (German): Verhältnis der beiden Seiten als Qualitäten
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › iii. Measure › α. Specific Quantity › b. Specifying Measure › iii. Relation of the Two Sides as Qualities
Gloss: The two sides of a measure, such as distance and time in a law of motion, each a distinct quality with its own amount.
Hegelian gloss: The two sides of a measure each a quality with its own quantum, bound by a determinate ratio, as space and time in fall.
Nouns: relation of the two sides as qualities; law of nature, physical law, formula, equation, function, correlation, dependence, covariation; space and time in falling, distance and duration; dimensions, variables, parameters, quantities, terms; dimensional analysis. the two sides as qualities, the qualitative sides of measure, space and time in motion, the law of fall.

Adjective: functional, correlative, covariant, dimensional, lawful, law-governed. qualitative, two-sided, correlated.
Adverbs: as a function of, in terms of, in relation to. on both sides, qualitatively.
Phrases: s = ½gt²; in step; keep pace with.
Hegel definition: In the relation of the two sides as qualities, the external quantum that was merely specified is shown to be the quantum of a something with its own quality, so that both sides are qualitative existences for themselves, each with its specific magnitude. Their relation is determined by an exponent of measure, and the quantities are so interwoven that the qualities are determined only through them, as indivisible. Measure is here the immanent quantitative relation of two qualities to each other, as of space and time in the motion of bodies.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Measure › Specific quantity › Specifying measure › Relation of the two sides as qualities
Hegel citations:
The two sides thus stand to each other in a qualitative respect, each a qualitative existence for itself
— The Science of Logic, Specifying measure › Relation of the two sides as qualities (tr. di Giovanni)
Measure is thus the immanent quantitative relating of two qualities to each other.
— The Science of Logic, Specifying measure › Relation of the two sides as qualities (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Being-for-Self in Measure
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › iii. Measure › α. Specific Quantity › c. Being-for-Self in Measure
Gloss: A measure that maintains itself as a constant relation; a stable proportion that defines a thing.

Hegel definition: Being-for-itself in measure arises where the qualitative moment, still immediate and with a magnitude of its own, is bound to its specific relation of measure. In any such relation, as in the law of falling bodies, there is an empirical coefficient, an immediate quantum not derived from the law, which is the being-for-itself of the measure, though only as immediate. As the unity of its two sides, one immediate and external and the other specified within, measure becomes complete self-subsistence: a something which is the unity of qualities in a relation of measure.

The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Measure › Specific quantity › The being-for-itself in measure
Hegel citations:
Here we are only concerned with this conceptual determination, namely that in any determination of measure the empirical coefficient constitutes the being-for-itself, but only the moment of the being-for-itself, in so far as it is in principle and therefore as immediate.
— The Science of Logic, Specific quantity › The being-for-itself in measure (tr. di Giovanni)
This negative unity is real being-for-itself, the category of a something which is the unity of qualities in a relation of measure – a complete self-subsistence.
— The Science of Logic, Specific quantity › The being-for-itself in measure (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Real Measure
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › iii. Measure › β. Real Measure
Gloss: Measure embodied in an independent thing that is itself a set of proportions.
Hegelian gloss: Measure become a self-subsistent something, which is itself a unity of measures in ratio to others.
Nouns: real measure; independent measure, self-subsistent measure, real thing as measure, body, material thing, specific substance; proportioned thing, embodied ratio, physical body with constants; substance, material; compound, alloy, mixture. matter, stuff. amalgam, composition. thing, object. embodied measure, the measure of independent things, physical measure, specific gravity.

Adjective: real, material, substantial, self-subsistent, independent, bodily, concrete, proportioned. physical. corporeal. dense, solid, compact, massive. embodied.

Hegel definition: Real measure is measure determined as a connection of the measures that make up the quality of distinct self-subsisting somethings, or things: no longer abstract qualities such as space and time, but specific gravity and chemical properties. Such an independent measure relates to others and specifies them, forming a series of measures. Some of these relations are exclusive elective affinities, which form a nodal line of self-subsisting things, and out of the progression there emerges the measureless, in which anything self-subsisting stands in negative relation to itself.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Measure › Real measure
Hegel citations:
Measure is now determined as a connection of measures that make up the quality of distinct self-subsisting somethings
— The Science of Logic, Measure › Real measure (tr. di Giovanni)
Third, what emerges in this progression for measure, however, is the measureless: the measureless in general and more specifically the infinitude of measure in which the mutually exclusive forms of self-subsistence are one with each other, and anything self-subsistent comes to stand in negative reference to itself.
— The Science of Logic, Measure › Real measure (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: The Relation of Self-Subsistent Measures
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › iii. Measure › β. Real Measure › a. The Relation of Self-Subsistent Measures

Hegel definition: The relation of independent measures concerns measures that have become self-subsisting because within themselves they are specified relations, so that they are things, physical and at first material. At first the two sides subsist in things external to each other and are combined externally. Yet these material beings are what they are qualitatively only through their quantitative determination as measures, and through it they are related to others in a series, their affinity, until one relation cuts itself off exclusively as elective affinity.

The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Being › Measure › Real measure › The relation of independent measures
Hegel citations:
By measures we no longer mean now merely immediate measures, but measures that are self-subsistent because they become within themselves relations which are specified, and in this being-for-itself they are thus a something, things that are physical and at first material.
— The Science of Logic, Real measure › The relation of independent measures (tr. di Giovanni)
But the self-subsistent materialities are what they qualitatively are only in virtue of the quantitative determination that they have as measures
— The Science of Logic, Real measure › The relation of independent measures (tr. di Giovanni)

Hegel definition: A nodal line of measures is the series formed when one and the same substrate, in the course of merely quantitative increase and decrease, reaches points at which the altered quantity suddenly becomes a new measure, a new quality, a new something. Up to such a point there is a margin within which the quality is indifferent to the change. The new quality does not grow gradually out of the old: gradualness concerns only the external side of the alteration, and on the qualitative side it is broken off by a leap. But there comes a point in the quantitative alteration at which this quality alters and the quantum shows itself to be specifying, so that the altered quantitative relation is suddenly turned into a measure and thereby into a new quality, a new something.
— The Science of Logic, Real measure › Nodal lines of measure-relations (tr. di Giovanni)
From the qualitative side, therefore, the gradual, merely quantitative progression which has no limits in itself, is absolutely interrupted; and since in its merely quantitative connection the newly emerging quality is with respect to the vanishing one an indeterminate other, one which is indifferent to it, the transition is a leap; the two are posited as wholly external to each other.
— The Science of Logic, Real measure › Nodal lines of measure-relations (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: The Becoming of Essence
Path: 一. Logic › 1. Doctrine of Being › iii. Measure › γ. The Becoming of Essence
Gloss: The process in which the shifting of measures reveals something underlying that persists through them.
Hegelian gloss: The sublation of measure into the indifferent substrate that persists through its alterations: essence in becoming.
Nouns: the becoming of essence; inwardization, internalization; going within, introversion, deepening, profundity, depth; penetration, getting to the bottom, finding the core; disclosure of the substrate; the depth beneath the surface, the essential behind the given; transition to essence &c H0087. the genesis of essence, the emergence of essence, the passage of measure into essence, the underlying revealed. hypokeimenon.

Hegel definition: The becoming of essence is the movement in which being, through measure, passes into essence. Being first becomes absolute indifference, mediating itself into a simple unity through the negation of every determinateness of quality, quantity and measure, with these as mere states of a substrate. This indifference proves a contradiction: it repels itself from itself in an infinite negative self-reference, so that its determinations are no longer self-subsisting but only posited, referred to their unity. Being which, through the sublation of being, is simple being with itself is essence.

The indifference which can be called absolute, however, is one which, through the negation of every determinateness of being, of quality and quantity and of their at first immediate unity, that is, of measure, mediates itself with itself to form a simple unity.

Indifference, now posited as what it in fact is, is simple and infinitely negative self-reference, the incompatibility of itself with itself, the repelling of itself from itself.
— The Science of Logic, Measure › The becoming of essence (tr. di Giovanni)
And so is being determined as essence – being which, through the sublation of being, is simple being with itself.
— The Science of Logic, Measure › The becoming of essence (tr. di Giovanni)

Hegel definition: Reflection is shine taken back from its immediacy: the movement of becoming and passing over that remains within itself, in which what is distinguished is only the negative in itself. Hegel definition: The determinations of reflection, or essentialities, are essence as determined, the distinct moments across which it moves and in which it shines, each reflected into itself. They have customarily been set up as universal laws of thought, such as that everything is equal to itself, but they are no qualitative determinacies that could simply stand side by side.

It is not the equality of being, nor what is left by an abstraction that sets difference aside outside it, but a pure production of unity from and in itself. Identity held apart from difference is the product of external reflection; in truth everything that is self-identical is in that identity also different and contradictory.
Hegel texts:
The Science of Logic
· The Doctrine of Essence › The determinations of reflection › Identity
Hegel citations:
Essence is simple immediacy as sublated immediacy. Its negativity is its being; it is equal to itself in its absolute negativity by virtue of which otherness and reference to other have as such simply disappeared into pure self-equality. Essence is therefore simple self-identity.
— The Science of Logic, The determinations of reflection › Identity (tr. di Giovanni)
It is not that self-equality which being is, or also nothing, but a self-equality which, in producing itself as unity, does not produce itself over again, as from another, but is a pure production, from itself and in itself, essential identity.
— The Science of Logic, The determinations of reflection › Identity (tr. di Giovanni)
Contrary to this, the identity that stays distant from difference, and the difference that stays distant from identity, are the products of external reflection and of an abstraction that arbitrarily clings to this point of indifferent difference.
— The Science of Logic, The determinations of reflection › Identity, Remark (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Difference

Gloss: Distinction; a thing's not being the same as another, or as itself in another respect.

As self-referring it is difference of itself from itself, and so it is both itself and identity: difference is the whole and its own moment, just as identity is. — The Science of Logic, The determinations of reflection › Difference (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Absolute Difference
Path: 一. Logic › 2. Doctrine of Essence › i. Essence as Reflection Within Itself › β. Determinations of Reflection › b. Difference › i. Absolute Difference
Gloss: Difference as such, considered by itself rather than as a difference between particular things.
Hegelian gloss: Difference in and for itself, the difference of essence, which is only as related to identity.
Nouns: absolute difference; difference as such, pure difference, difference in itself, self-related difference, simple difference, otherness as such; the negative, negativity; radical difference, absolute otherness, wholly other; incommensurability. the difference of essence.

Hegel definition: Absolute difference is difference in and for itself, the difference of essence. It is not made by something external but refers to itself and is therefore simple: in the difference of A and not-A it is the simple "not" that constitutes it. It is not the otherness of existence, where two things lie outside each other and each is something immediate for itself; the other of essence is the other in and for itself, simple determinateness in itself. As difference from itself, it contains identity.

In the absolute difference of A and not-A from each other, it is the simple “not” which, as such, constitutes the difference.
— The Science of Logic, Difference › Absolute difference (tr. di Giovanni)
The other of essence, by contrast, is the other in and for itself, not the other of some other which is to be found outside it; it is simple determinateness in itself.
— The Science of Logic, Difference › Absolute difference (tr. di Giovanni)

Hegel definition: Diversity is identity broken apart: its moments, identity and difference, are each reflected into itself and so subsist indifferent to one another, the diverse remaining what it is. Since neither is referred to the other, the difference is external to them, and they are merely different in general. — The Science of Logic, Difference › Diversity (tr. di Giovanni)

Gloss: Difference in which each side is defined by the other as its opposite, as positive and negative, north and south.

Hegel definition: Opposition is the determinate reflection, difference, brought to completion: the unity of identity and diversity, whose moments are diverse within one identity and so opposed. Each side contains its relation to its non-being and is the whole only through it. Likeness reflected into itself and containing the reference to unlikeness is the positive; unlikeness containing the reference to likeness is the negative. Each has the other in it, and each becomes a self-subsisting side of the opposition.

— The Science of Logic, Difference › Opposition (tr. di Giovanni)

Head: Contradiction
Path: 一. Logic › 2. Doctrine of Essence › i. Essence as Reflection Within Itself › β. Determinations of Reflection › c. Contradiction

Phrases: do I contradict myself? Very well then I contradict myself [Whitman]; polemos patēr pantōn [Gr.] [war is the father of all] [Heraclitus]; all things are in themselves contradictory [Hegel]; credo quia absurdum [Lat.]; spear and shield, maodun [Chin.] [Han Feizi]; a contradiction in terms; to fly in the face of; asinus ad lyram [Lat.]; misfortune is what fortune leans on, fortune is where misfortune hides, huo xi fu suo yi, fu xi huo suo fu [Chin.] [Laozi].
Hegel definition: Contradiction arises because each side of opposition is self-subsisting only by containing the other and excluding it in the same respect, so that in its very self-subsistence it excludes its own self-subsistence. Difference is already implicitly this, and the positive and negative are contradiction posited. It resolves itself: the opposites ceaselessly pass over into each other and vanish, yet the result is not only nothing. In sublating its own positedness, opposition goes to ground, and what emerges is essence as a unity with itself.

Matter is simple identity without distinction, the other of form and its substrate, what is left when every form of a thing is abstracted away, and so is never seen or felt except as determinate matter. Hegel definition: Determinate ground is ground that has a content. A content, indifferent to the form of the connection, serves as the substrate in which ground and grounded are one, and the determinateness of that content gives the ground its definiteness. Head: Real Ground
Path: 一. Logic › 2. Doctrine of Essence › i. Essence as Reflection Within Itself › γ. Ground › b. Determinate Ground › ii. Real Ground

Hegel definition: Real ground is ground in which ground and grounded have different contents, so that the connection ceases to be a tautology: whoever asks for a ground now demands another determination of content than the one whose ground is sought. Since the two determinations are indifferent to each other, their unity is only an empty linking by a something that holds them together from outside, and so the connection is no true mediation.

Gloss: Being that has come forth from a basis; actual presence that has reasons behind it.
Hegelian gloss: The immediacy of being restored by the sublation of mediation: being that has come forth from ground.
Nouns: existence; ex-istence, standing forth, emergence from ground; actual existence, concrete existence, real existence, being in the world, worldly existence, actuality &c H0136; the existent, existing things, entities, the furniture of the world. reality, actuality, positiveness, fact, matter of fact, sober reality, truth &c H0214. grounded being, the emerged. extancy. secondness [Peirce].
Verbs: exist, be, subsist, obtain, live, stand forth, issue, emerge, come forth. have being, breathe, stand, be the case, occur &c H0116, have place, prevail, find oneself, pass the time, vegetate. come into existence, come to pass. persist, endure, abide. emanate, come out of. subsist &c H0004. arise &c H0009, come forth &c H0418.
Adjective: existent, existing, extant, actual, real, concrete, worldly, factual, live, living. under the sun, afloat, afoot, on foot, current, prevalent, undestroyed. present. positive, absolute, true &c H0214, substantial, substantive, self-existing, self-existent, essential. actual &c H0004. grounded.
Adverbs: in existence, in being, in actuality, in fact.
Foreign: German: das Existierende; Latin: existentia, in esse, de facto, esse et id quod est [being and that-which-is] [Boethius]; Greek: hyparxis; Arabic: wujūd [existence].
Phrases: existence precedes essence, l'existence précède l'essence [Fr.] [Sartre]; as large as life.
Hegel definition: Concrete existence is essence that has come forth into immediacy. The truth of being is not to be an immediate something but this: whatever is, exists concretely. It proceeds from ground and condition by sublating the mediation between them, so that it may be said both to have a ground and to have none. It is the second kind of being, after immediate being, and it is not the product of a proof or a derivation from outside but the movement of the fact itself. As negative unity it is a thing.
Hegel texts:
